title: Execute rule actions through the OMS under the per-rule safety limits
body:
## Context
US-RULE-003 requires the full action vocabulary to actually work, and its NFR states "every action is idempotent or explicitly marked non-idempotent with a guard; all actions audited with the triggering rule and evaluation snapshot". This is where a rule stops being an opinion and becomes an order.

Two structural decisions from `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.7 govern the design and are non-negotiable: **profile risk caps are enforced by the OMS *after* the rule engine, so no rule can exceed them**, and the native exchange-side stop-loss invariant (ADR-0008) is untouchable — "no rule may remove the native exchange SL" (ADR-0007 binding rule 7), and smarter stops layered on top "may only ever tighten the native stop, never loosen or remove it" unless the user explicitly overrides with an audited confirmation.

Transactionality is deliberately weak and must be implemented as specified rather than improved upon: §11.5 E9 says with `on_error="abort_remaining"` (default) a failed action stops the remaining actions in that fire, everything already done is recorded, **nothing is rolled back** (you cannot un-place a filled order), and the partial outcome is alerted. Inventing a rollback here would be worse than the honest partial state.

## Scope / Deliverables
- An `ActionExecutor` implementing all 25 action types from `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.2/§11.6, each validated against its per-action parameter schema (E35-T03) and dispatched through the **M14 OMS** (E29) — never directly to the exchange adapter:
  `place_order`, `modify_stop_loss`, `modify_take_profit`, `cancel_order`, `cancel_all_orders`, `move_to_breakeven`, `scale_out`, `scale_in`, `flatten_position`, `flatten_all_positions`, `reverse_position`, `halt_new_orders`, `resume_new_orders`, `reduce_leverage`, `widen_stop`, `tighten_stop`, `arm_chase_limit`, `start_iceberg_slice`, `start_twap`, `send_notification`, `log_journal_tag`, `set_variable`, `emit_signal`, `pause_rule`, `enable_rule`.
- Ordered, deterministic execution (E5) with `on_error` semantics `abort_remaining` (default), `continue`, `retry_once`.
- **Idempotency**: each action derives a stable dedupe key from `(rule_id, version, scope_instance, node_id, fire_sequence)`, which becomes the OMS `orderLinkId` seed for order-placing actions so a retry or a reconnect cannot double-place.
- **Safety limits before execution** (§11.7): `max_actions_per_fire`, `max_notional_per_fire`, `max_daily_notional`, the `rules_global_enabled` feature flag, and the **kill-switch** — an engaged kill-switch blocks every rule action, and `PUT /api/v1/system/kill-switch` also disarms armed rules (E39).
- `require_confirmation`: queue the fire for human confirmation with a 60 s TTL, surfaced to the UI, expiring silently-but-logged if unanswered.
- **Stop-safety clamps**: `only_tighten` defaults true on `modify_stop_loss`/`modify_take_profit`; `only_tighten=false` and `widen_stop` require the `rules.loosen_stop` permission plus the Owner role, and are audited at high severity. No action path can remove the native SL.
- `exclude_algo_children` (E11, default true): no rule may act on another rule's or algo's child orders.
- The rule-scoped variable store backing `set_variable` (name, value, `ttl_ms`) and the signal bus backing `emit_signal`/`on_signal`, with a chain-depth limit so signal chains cannot become an infinite loop.
- `ActionResult` records feeding the firing log (E35-S06), including `blocked_by`/`blocked_detail` when a cap or permission stopped the action.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the OMS operations themselves — **E29**; brackets and native-SL enforcement — **E32**; emulated algos (`arm_chase_limit`, `start_iceberg_slice`, `start_twap` bodies) — **E33**; fan-out across accounts — **E34**. This story calls them.
- The kill-switch itself and risk-cap computation — **E39**; this story honours both.
- Notification delivery channels — **E40**; `send_notification` hands off to it.
- Simulated execution — **E35-S05** (which swaps the sink, not the path).
- Journal write-back beyond emitting the tag — **E41**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Actions run in order and stop on failure by default
  Given a fire with three actions and on_error abort_remaining
  When the second action fails
  Then the first action's effect is recorded, the third is never attempted, nothing is rolled back
  And the partial outcome raises an alert naming the rule, the fire and the failed action

Scenario: A rule can never exceed the account's risk caps (failure case)
  Given an armed rule whose place_order would breach the per-account profile cap
  When the rule fires
  Then the OMS rejects the order after the rule engine has planned it
  And the rejection is recorded on the action with blocked_by naming the cap, and no order reaches the exchange

Scenario: No rule can remove or loosen a native stop (failure case)
  Given a rule attempting to widen a stop while the author lacks rules.loosen_stop or the Owner role
  When the action executes
  Then it is refused with a permission error, audited at high severity, and the native exchange-side stop is unchanged

Scenario: The kill-switch stops every rule action within its guarantee
  Given the global kill-switch is engaged
  When any armed rule fires
  Then every action is blocked before reaching the OMS, blocked_by records kill_switch
  And existing positions are untouched

Scenario: A retried fire does not double-place (edge case)
  Given an action whose OMS call timed out with an unknown outcome
  When the executor retries under on_error retry_once
  Then the same dedupe key is reused so the OMS resolves it to the original order rather than creating a second one

Scenario: Confirmation-required fires expire safely (edge case)
  Given a rule with require_confirmation true that fires
  When no human responds within 60 seconds
  Then the fire expires without executing, the expiry is logged with its reason, and no action is taken later

Scenario: Signal chains are bounded (failure case)
  Given rule A emitting a signal that triggers rule B, which emits a signal triggering rule A
  When A fires
  Then the chain stops at the configured depth limit, the truncation is logged as an error, and neither rule loops
```

## Technical notes / design
Dispatch table keyed on `Action.type` with one handler per type; each handler declares `idempotent: bool` and, when false, the guard it relies on, so the US-RULE-003 NFR is structurally satisfied rather than asserted in prose. A new action type cannot be added without both, enforced by a completeness test.

`targets` resolution (§11.2): `scope_accounts` (default) uses the rule's scope, `originating_account` uses the account of the triggering event, `all_accounts` requires the widest permission and is audited. Resolution happens **before** the per-action permission check, and the resolved account list is recorded on the `ActionResult` so the log shows exactly who was affected.

Order-placing actions go through the full trade-group path including sizing and native SL (§11.6 table note on `place_order`) — the rule engine supplies intent, the OMS supplies sizing from the per-account profile (E28) and the mandatory native stop (E32). The engine must **not** compute quantities itself when `qty_mode` refers to a profile; doing so would duplicate and eventually diverge from the profile logic.

`pause_rule`/`enable_rule` cannot target themselves except `pause_rule` (self-disable is allowed and useful — §11.6). Enforce at execution as well as validation, because scope resolution can make a target dynamic.

The confirmation queue is persisted, not in-memory: a backend restart during the 60 s TTL must expire the fire rather than resurrect it, because the market state that justified it is gone.

## Test plan
Unit (>=90%): one handler test per action type including parameter validation failure; `on_error` matrix across the three modes; dedupe-key derivation stability; `targets` resolution for the three modes; `only_tighten` clamp in both directions; self-targeting guards; confirmation TTL expiry including the restart case; signal chain-depth limit.
Safety suite (a **required check** per roadmap §7.4, failing merges rather than only releases): no action path can produce an OMS call that removes a native SL; kill-switch blocks all 25 action types; an over-cap order is rejected by the OMS and recorded, not silently dropped.
Integration against the OMS with recorded Bybit demo fixtures: partial fill mid-action, rejection with `10001`, rate-limit `10018`, WS disconnect between two actions of one fire.
Chaos: backend restart mid-fire — extended in **E35-Q05**.
Contract: `ActionResult` and `SimulatedAction` shapes against `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.9.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

This is the highest-risk ticket in the epic and is automatically `security`-labelled under `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 (it touches `area/oms-execution` order-placement paths). Mandatory controls, each with a negative test: per-action permission checks evaluated **at execution time** against the current grants, not the grants at authoring time; `rules.loosen_stop` plus Owner role for any stop-widening; the native-SL invariant; the kill-switch check as the last gate before the OMS call; `max_notional_per_fire`/`max_daily_notional` enforced server-side; and an audit record per action carrying the triggering rule, version, `ir_hash` and the evaluation snapshot. A manual abuse-case check is required before Done: craft a rule that attempts, by each available action, to open a position without a native SL, and confirm all attempts are rejected, logged and audited (R3 exit criterion 2).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The `blocked_by`/`blocked_detail` strings become user-facing text in SCR-084 and SCR-087 and must be written as plain-language explanations of what stopped the action and what to change.

## Performance notes
Action dispatch overhead must be negligible against the order submit -> ack p95 <300 ms gate (budget #4): target <=10 ms from fire decision to OMS submit call, measured. `flatten_all_positions` and `cancel_all_orders` fan across accounts through the OMS's own rate-limit governor (E34) and must not bypass it.

## Observability
`rule_actions_total{type,result}` where result is ok|failed|blocked|skipped, `rule_action_duration_seconds{type}`, `rule_actions_blocked_total{reason}` (cap|permission|kill_switch|native_sl|confirmation_expired), `rule_signal_chain_truncated_total`. Audit per action: actor is the rule, with `rule_id`, `version`, `ir_hash`, `run_id`, resolved accounts, parameters and outcome. A `critical` alert on any partial-fire outcome.

title: Enforce rule scope on every action at runtime, not only at save time
body:
## Context
US-RULE-007 gives a rule author scope control over accounts, symbols and positions, and its NFR is unusually explicit: **"scope is enforced at runtime on every action, not only at save time"**. The reason is a real attack and a real accident: a rule authored while the user held a grant must stop acting the moment that grant is revoked, an account is disabled, or a manager is frozen — waiting for someone to re-save the rule is not acceptable.

The second scenario in US-RULE-007 is equally pointed: an account the user cannot trade "is not listed at all, and a crafted API request is rejected with 403" — the UI filter is a convenience, the server check is the control.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A `ScopeResolver` that, for each evaluation and again for each action, resolves the rule's `RuleScope` (`level`, `account_ids`, `symbols`, `applies_to`, `environments`, `exclude_algo_children`) against the **current** state of: the rule owner's grants, account enabled/frozen state, the account's allowed-symbol list from its profile (E28), the environment gate, and the manager-freeze state (E39).
- Per-scope-instance expansion: a symbol-scoped rule across three symbols yields three independent instances (§11.5 E6), each carrying its own `scope_instance` key used for `once`/cooldown/temporal state and for the log.
- Environment gating (§11.5 E12): `scope.environments` defaults to `["demo"]`; including `"live"` requires the `rules.arm_live` permission, a confirmation, and a high-severity audit entry. An armed rule whose scope includes `live` while the live gate is closed in the backend configuration layer (M1) must not act on live, regardless of its IR.
- Scope-summary derivation for the UI header chip, e.g. `"2 accounts · BTCUSDT · new positions"` (US-RULE-007 scenario 3) — computed server-side so the summary can never disagree with what is enforced.
- 403 on crafted requests naming an out-of-permission account, with no information leak about whether the account exists.
- Revocation responsiveness: a grant revoked while a rule is armed takes effect on the next evaluation, and the affected scope instance is recorded as suppressed with `skipped_reason="scope"` rather than silently vanishing.

## Out of scope
- Account and grant management — **E27**/**E42**; profile allowed-symbol lists — **E28**; the manager freeze and kill-switch — **E39**. This story reads them.
- The scope selector UI (CMP-144 RuleScopeSelector) — E36.
- Action execution — **E35-S03** (which calls this resolver as its first gate).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Scope is re-checked on every action
  Given an armed rule scoped to accounts A and B
  And the author's grant on account B is revoked after the rule was armed
  When the rule next fires
  Then actions targeting A execute and actions targeting B are suppressed with skipped_reason scope
  And no re-save of the rule was required for this to take effect

Scenario: Out-of-permission account is invisible and unusable (failure case)
  Given a manager without a grant on account C
  When they list accounts for a rule scope, then craft an API request naming account C directly
  Then C is absent from the list and the crafted request is rejected with 403 without revealing whether C exists

Scenario: Live requires explicit opt-in (failure case)
  Given a rule whose scope.environments omits live
  When a live-environment trigger occurs
  Then the rule does not evaluate for that environment, and the skip is counted

Scenario: Per-symbol instances are independent (edge case)
  Given a symbol-scoped rule over BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT and SOLUSDT with once_per position
  When it fires for BTCUSDT
  Then the ETHUSDT and SOLUSDT instances remain eligible to fire, each with their own cooldown state

Scenario: A frozen manager's rules stop acting (failure case)
  Given a manager is frozen by the owner kill-switch
  When their armed rules next evaluate
  Then every action is suppressed with the freeze recorded as the reason, within the 2-second freeze guarantee
```

## Technical notes / design
Resolution is deliberately performed twice per fire — once to build the evaluation instances, once immediately before each action — because the window between them can contain a revocation, a freeze or an account disable. The second check is cheap (an in-memory grant snapshot refreshed on the auth/account event stream) so the cost is acceptable.

`applies_to` (`open_positions`/`pending_orders`/`account`/`any`) narrows which entities an action may touch: an `open_positions` rule must not cancel a pending order, and the resolver, not each action handler, is where that is enforced — otherwise 25 handlers each get it slightly wrong.

`exclude_algo_children` (default true, §11.5 E11) is resolved here: child orders created by emulated algos (E33) or by another rule carry their parent reference and are filtered out of the actionable set.

The 403 must be indistinguishable from 404 in its information content for accounts the caller cannot see — return the standard problem document without confirming existence, matching the RBAC matrix test in R3 exit criterion 10 which asserts "403 + no state change + audit row for every disallowed combination".

## Test plan
Unit (>=90%): resolution matrix over `level` x `applies_to` x grant state x account state x environment; `exclude_algo_children` filtering; scope-summary string generation for each shape.
Security tests: crafted request naming an ungranted account (403, no state change, audit row written); grant revoked between evaluation and action; manager frozen mid-fire; live-environment attempt with the live gate closed.
Integration: three-symbol instance isolation with independent `once_per=position` state; revocation during an armed rule's lifetime.
Contract: the scope summary returned by the rules API matches the enforced scope, asserted by a property test — the summary can never claim a wider or narrower scope than what the resolver permits.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

This story *is* a security control. It is the elevation-of-privilege mitigation named in the epic's STRIDE model (E35-X01) and feeds the RBAC matrix test in R3 exit criterion 10. Every disallowed combination must produce 403, no state change and an audit row. The account-existence non-disclosure requirement is explicit. Because grants are cached in memory for speed, the cache invalidation path (on grant change, account disable, freeze) is itself security-critical and needs a test proving a revocation is visible to the engine within one evaluation cycle.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The scope-summary string it produces is rendered as the rule header chip and is read by screen readers, so it must be a complete sentence-like phrase, not an abbreviation cluster.

## Performance notes
Resolution must not dominate evaluation: target <=2 ms per fire for a rule scoped to 5 accounts and 10 symbols, achieved by an in-memory grant/account snapshot invalidated on the auth and account event streams rather than a database round trip per action.

## Observability
`rule_scope_suppressions_total{reason}` (grant_revoked|account_disabled|frozen|environment|allowed_symbols|algo_child), `rule_scope_resolution_duration_seconds`. Every suppression is a `rule_events` row with `kind=throttled` or an explicit suppression kind, so US-RULE-010's "suppressed firing is logged too" requirement is satisfied here rather than being forgotten.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage: rule-engine package >=90% line (R3 local policy, roadmap §7.4), other backend >=85%, frontend >=80%; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated where behaviour diverged: `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11, `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4; ADR-0007 amended if an IR semantic changed.

- [ ] PR(s) <=400 LOC diff, merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`rules_global_enabled`; `rules.graph_editor` where relevant).

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E35-S02**. Reads grants from **E09**, accounts from **E27**, allowed symbols from **E28**, freeze state from **E39**, algo-child lineage from **E33**/**E29**. Gates **E35-S03**.

title: Run rules in simulate mode and auto-backtest them on save
body:
## Context
US-RULE-008 makes simulate-only mode the trust-building on-ramp, and its NFR is the whole design in one line: **"simulate mode shares the identical evaluation path as live — only the action sink differs."** §11.7's new-rule gate makes this mandatory rather than optional: a newly created or edited rule cannot be armed directly; it must run in `simulate` for `min_simulation_fires` (default 5) or `min_simulation_hours` (default 24), whichever comes first.

US-RULE-009 (Should) adds auto-backtest on save over recorded history, with the same NFR shape: "backtest uses the same engine and ingestion path as live and replay". `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.9 notes simulation also runs against replay (§13.7): "point a rule at a recorded window and get the same `RuleEvent` stream you would have got live, because the metrics are deterministic and the engine reads the same bus".

Honesty about coverage is a first-class requirement: SCR-084 demands the panel state "history available: 13 of 14 days (recording started 09-01)" rather than silently returning a shorter series, and carries the required caveat copy "Simulation replays recorded market data. Fills are modelled, not real; results are not a guarantee."

## Scope / Deliverables
- A **simulated action sink** implementing `SimulatedAction` (`24-internal-schemas.md` §11.9): `action_type`, `params`, `would_target_accounts`, `estimated_qty`, `estimated_notional`, `estimated_price` (from the book at snapshot time), `estimated_fee`, `blocked_by`, `blocked_detail`. The evaluation path above it is byte-identical to live — a single injected sink, not a parallel code path. A test asserts the two paths share the same call graph.
- `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/simulate` accepting either a `from`/`to` history window or a `replay_session_id`, returning `RuleSimulationResult` synchronously for short windows and `202` with a `run_id` for long ones, with progress streamed on the `rules` WS topic and results readable from `GET /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/runs`.
- Result contents per the OpenAPI example: `evaluations`, `fires`, `suppressed_by_guard`, the per-action timeline with `would_have_succeeded`, `hypothetical_pnl_delta_usd`, `errors`, `duration_ms`.
- **Coverage honesty**: report the true covered range against the requested range, name the missing windows explicitly, and surface the no-history case with the recorder dependency (SCR-084 states `partial` and `no-history` as designed states).
- Hypothetical fills priced by the **paper matcher** (E38, §12) so simulation and paper trading agree; where the matcher is unavailable, degrade to mid-price with the limitation stated in the result, never silently.
- **Auto-backtest on save** (US-RULE-009): on `PUT /rules/{ruleId}`, evaluate over the configured lookback and store `backtest_summary` on the `rule_versions` row; run in the background with progress and a completion notification when it would exceed 30 seconds.
- Cancellation: a running simulation is cancellable and the cancellation is audited (`rule.simulation_cancelled`).
- The armed-gate bookkeeping: record which `ir_hash` a completed simulation covered, which is what `PUT /rules/{id}/mode` checks in E35-S01.
- Visual distinction data: simulated actions carry a flag so the chart and logs can render them distinctly and "can never be mistaken for real ones" (US-RULE-008 scenario 2).

## Out of scope
- The simulation panel UI (SCR-084) — **E35-S08**.
- The replay engine and its scrubbing — **E26**; the paper matcher fill model — **E38**. This story consumes both.
- Strategy backtesting as a product (P&L optimisation, parameter sweeps) — out of scope for v1 entirely; this is a rule-behaviour preview, not a backtester.
- The recorder — **E16**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Simulation touches nothing
  Given a rule armed in simulate-only mode
  When it fires
  Then every firing is recorded with the would-be action and its inputs
  And no exchange call is made by any path

Scenario: Simulate and live share one evaluation path
  Given the same recorded window evaluated once with the live sink stubbed and once with the simulated sink
  When both runs complete
  Then the sequence of condition traces and planned actions is identical, differing only in the sink's recorded outcome

Scenario: Coverage is reported honestly (edge case)
  Given a requested 14-day window where the recorder covers 13 days
  When the simulation runs
  Then it evaluates over what exists and the result states the true covered range and names the missing window

Scenario: No history at all (failure case)
  Given a symbol that has never been recorded
  When a simulation is requested
  Then it fails with a clear no-history result naming the symbol and the recorder action that would fix it, rather than returning zero fires as if the rule never matched

Scenario: Long simulations move to the background
  Given a simulation that would exceed 30 seconds
  When it is started
  Then a 202 with a run_id is returned, progress streams on the rules topic, and a notification fires on completion

Scenario: Promotion to live is gated and audited
  Given a simulated rule the user wants to arm
  When they promote it
  Then step-up authentication is required and the promotion is audited
  And promotion is refused unless a completed simulation exists for that exact ir_hash

Scenario: Determinism over replay
  Given the same replay session simulated three times
  When the runs complete
  Then the fires, their timestamps and their planned actions are identical across all three
```

## Technical notes / design
The single-sink design is the entire point and must be enforced structurally: the evaluator (E35-S02) and executor (E35-S03) take an `ActionSink` protocol; `LiveSink` calls the OMS, `SimulatedSink` records. There must be no `if simulate:` branch anywhere inside evaluation — a lint/architecture test asserts the string does not appear in the evaluator package, because that branch is exactly how simulation parity rots.

Simulation over replay drives the engine from the replay clock rather than wall time, so `on_timer`/`on_schedule` triggers fire on virtual time. This is why the scheduler in E35-S02 is injected rather than global.

`hypothetical_pnl_delta_usd` is explicitly a **modelled** number. Label it as such in the payload and never present it as a backtest result; SCR-084's required caveat copy exists precisely to prevent that misreading, and R12 (backtest bias) is the risk being managed.

Auto-backtest on save must not make saving slow: run it asynchronously and write `backtest_summary` when it completes; the save returns immediately with the new version. A save whose backtest is still running shows as pending rather than blocking the editor.

## Test plan
Unit (>=90%): sink protocol substitution; `SimulatedAction` field derivation incl. `blocked_by` when a cap would have stopped it; coverage-range computation against gapped recordings; the 30-second async threshold; cancellation mid-run.
Parity test (the important one): run an identical window through both sinks and assert identical condition traces and planned actions.
Determinism: three identical replay runs produce identical results — this is R3 exit criterion 6 and is extended by **E35-Q03**.
Integration: against E26 replay fixtures with a known gap; against the E38 paper matcher for fill pricing; a 14-day single-symbol window for the perf budget.
Contract: `SimulateRuleRequest`, `RuleSimulationResult` and the `202` shape against `22-api-openapi.yaml`, including the documented example verbatim.
Negative: assert via a network-level spy that **zero** exchange calls occur during any simulation.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

Specific to this ticket: the "no exchange call in simulate mode" property must be proven by a test that fails if an exchange client is ever constructed during a simulation, not merely by code reading — this is the control that lets a user trust the preview. Promotion from simulate to armed is a privileged transition requiring step-up authentication and an audit record (US-RULE-008 scenario 3). Simulation results are evidence used to justify arming, so `rule.simulation_started|completed|cancelled` are **audited**, not merely analytics (SCR-084). Simulation is also a resource-exhaustion surface: cap concurrent simulations per user and bound the requested window.

## Accessibility notes
Backend, but it produces the content of SCR-084: the coverage statement, the caveat copy and the per-firing timeline all need text that stands alone for a screen reader. The timeline must be expressible as a table (SCR-084: "results are a table; the timeline has a text list equivalent"), so the API returns structured rows rather than a pre-formatted narrative.

## Performance notes
Budget from SCR-084: 14 days of one symbol at 1-minute granularity completes in <=60 s, with partial results streamed as they are produced and the UI fully interactive throughout. Progress updates on the `rules` topic at the topic's 250 ms cadence. Concurrent simulations are bounded and queued rather than allowed to starve the live evaluator — the live path has absolute priority.

## Observability
`rule_simulations_total{result}`, `rule_simulation_duration_seconds`, `rule_simulation_evaluations_total`, `rule_simulation_coverage_ratio`. Audit: `rule.simulation_started {ruleId, range, symbol, accountId}`, `rule.simulation_completed {fires, actions, errors, durationMs}`, `rule.simulation_cancelled`.

title: Persist the firing log and publish rule state on the rules WS topic
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** Rule state published on the rules WS topic is read directly from the `B9` (`rule_instance`) machine's published enum; no estimate change.

US-RULE-010 requires a log of every evaluation-relevant event, including **suppressed** firings and their reason, with an NFR that is stronger than typical logging: "log retained indefinitely (it is part of the audit trail); a firing's snapshot is sufficient to reproduce the decision." ADR-0007 binding rule 4 says the same from the engineering side: "Every evaluation is logged — including no-ops — with the values of every metric that was read. Without this, a rule that fires wrongly is un-debuggable."

That collides with physics: a 250 ms evaluator produces roughly 345 000 evaluations per day per rule. `21-database-schema.md` §3.4.3 resolves the collision explicitly — a `rule_runs` row is persisted only when `matched = true`, when `status = 'error'`, or when the rule is in `simulate` mode with the per-rule `rules.settings.record_all` flag set; non-persisted evaluations are counted in Prometheus only. This story implements exactly that policy, not a more generous one.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Persist `rule_runs` per the policy above, with `input_snapshot` (the values the conditions saw, sufficient to replay the decision), `matched`, `actions_planned`, `actions_executed`, `trigger_reason`, `scope_account_id`, `scope_symbol`, `trade_group_id`, `error_code`/`error_message`, `duration_ms`.
- Persist `rule_events` rows in sequence per run: `condition_eval`, `action_start`, `action_ok`, `action_fail`, `throttled`, `log` — each with `node_ref` linking back to the IR node so the graph editor can highlight it, `payload` and `severity`.
- **Suppression logging**: a rule that would have fired but was stopped by a guard (cooldown, scope, risk cap, permission, kill-switch, stale data) records the suppression and its reason (US-RULE-010 scenario 2). This is the requirement most easily lost, and it has its own acceptance scenario.
- `GET /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/runs` (cursor paginated; filters `status`, `kind` live|simulation, `from`, `to`) and `GET /api/v1/rules/runs/{runId}/events` — "the debugging surface for why did/didn't my rule fire".
- Export of a filtered run set (US-RULE-010 scenario 3) in CSV, reusing the platform export path.
- **WS topic `rules`**: publish `RuleUpdate` frames per `23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6 at the 250 ms coalescing cadence, honouring the subscription options `rule_ids` and `include_events`. **Who receives a rule is #3488's rule, not grants alone:** a snapshot row or a delta reaches a non-Owner only for a rule `rule_visible` (`rules/manager.py`, the check behind `GET /rules`) shows them when the hub publishes the delta or builds the snapshot, on the principal as it is then (they own the rule and every account any version names is still among their view grants; the Owner role reads every rule; a deleted rule, no one). Deltas go out one rule per `SequencingHub.publish(..., viewer=)`, the viewer being `ws_wiring.rule_frame_visible` bound to that rule's row (the hub refuses a `rules` publish without a `viewer`); snapshot rows pass the same check; `exchange_account_ids` and `rule_ids` only narrow further. Snapshot + delta per the protocol's standard shape; armed-state changes and fire counts update SCR-080 in place.
- Retention wiring to the job created in E35-T02 (7-day prune of non-matched, 24 months for matched, Parquet archive).
- Read rule state for the WS topic from the `B9` (`rule_instance`) chart's published enum via `statechart.factory` / `statechart.persistence`; do not maintain a parallel hand-rolled rule-state enum.
- All sends go through `statechart.gateway`.


## Out of scope
- The fire-history screen (SCR-087) — **E35-S09**.
- The audit log browser and hash-chain verification — **E42**; this story writes audit events, it does not build the browser.
- Conflict records — **E35-S07**.
- Parquet archive writer internals — **E16**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A firing is fully explainable
  Given an armed rule fires
  Then the log records timestamp, rule id and version, the metric snapshot, the action taken, the resulting exchange order ids and the outcome
  And the snapshot alone is sufficient to re-derive the same decision

Scenario: Suppressed firings are logged too
  Given a rule that would have fired but a guard suppressed it
  When the evaluation completes
  Then the suppression and its specific reason are recorded and visible in the run list

Scenario: Noise is counted, not stored (edge case)
  Given a rule evaluating every 250 ms without matching
  When an hour passes
  Then no rule_runs rows are written for those evaluations, the Prometheus evaluation counter reflects them all
  And a rule in simulate mode with record_all enabled does write them

Scenario: History is filterable and exportable
  When the log is filtered by rule, account or outcome
  Then results are filterable, keyboard navigable and exportable as CSV

Scenario: WS subscribers see only the rules they may read (failure case, #3488)
  Given a Manager granted account A, an Owner rule on A, an Owner rule naming no account and the Manager's own rule on A
  And the Manager subscribes to rules with rule_ids naming all three, and a second subscription names ids that do not exist
  When each of the three rules changes state, and again after the Manager's grant on A is revoked
  Then both subscriptions are established with the same answer
  And the Manager receives the snapshot row and every delta of their own rule only, never one of the Owner's two, and nothing for a rule that names A once the grant is gone
  And the Owner role receives all three, and no frame for a deleted rule reaches anyone

Scenario: Events are immutable (failure case)
  Given a persisted rule_events row
  When any process attempts to update or delete it
  Then the append-only trigger rejects the statement
```

## Technical notes / design
Writes are off the evaluation hot path: the evaluator emits `RuleEvent` objects to a bounded queue drained by a writer task, so a slow database cannot stall evaluation. If the queue saturates, drop **non-matched** simulate records first, then log a `rule_log_dropped_total` increment — never drop a matched run or an error, which are evidence.

`input_snapshot` must be bounded: store the metrics actually referenced by the rule, not the whole registry, and cap payload size with an explicit truncation marker so an unusually wide rule cannot produce multi-megabyte rows.

`node_ref` semantics follow ADR-0016's decision on node-id stability across versions (E35-K01) — the log stores the version too, so a historical event always resolves against the version it ran under rather than the current one.

The `rules` topic is a **private** topic and is flat, not per-entity: there is no `rules.{ruleId}` channel (`14-screens-catalogue.md` §0.2). Scoping is #3488's reading rule applied per rule when the hub publishes a delta or builds a snapshot (the options only narrow it), so one subscription covers everything the user may read. Snapshots are built per subscription from the connection's current principal (a read-through accessor on `Subscription`, which carries none today), and a grants change that alters what a user may read re-snapshots their `rules` subscriptions (`reconfigure`), because the §9.5 re-evaluation only acts when a subscription's own accounts change. A deleted rule is no one's and `RuleUpdate` has no tombstone, so a deletion re-snapshots the `rules` subscriptions of everyone who could read it (its owner and the Owner role) as well.
- Normative contract: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B9.1-.8. Mandatory config: 29-statechart-adoption-plan §1.2. The firing-log persistence stays plain code; only the rule *state* is chart-derived.


## Test plan
Unit (>=90%): persistence policy decision table (matched / error / simulate+record_all / plain no-op); suppression reason mapping; snapshot truncation; queue back-pressure behaviour incl. the drop order.
Contract: `/rules/{ruleId}/runs` and `/rules/runs/{runId}/events` against `22-api-openapi.yaml`; `RuleUpdate` frames against `cv://ws/v1/rules.schema.json` including snapshot-then-delta ordering and the 250 ms coalescing rule.
Integration (Postgres + WS): a 10-minute armed-rule run producing the expected row counts; append-only trigger rejection; retention prune boundary; a Manager's snapshot and deltas hold none of an Owner's rules, on a shared account or naming none, and a revoked grant ends delivery (`test_ws_rules_revoked_grant_stops_events`, `test_ws_rules_omits_foreign_rule_ids`); each publish carries one rule.
Perf: sustained write throughput at the worst-case matched rate without lock contention; the SCR-087 query plan verified against the partial indexes.
- contract-suite membership (`tests/xstate_contract/test_b09_rule_instance.py`) verifying the WS-published state matches the chart enum on every transition


## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

Specific to this ticket: the firing log is the epic's non-repudiation control, so the append-only trigger must be verified by test, not assumed. `rule_runs.input_snapshot` carries account equity and position data — **financial/confidential**; it is served only under `rules:read` with account scoping and must not appear in shared log sinks. The WS subscription-option intersection is an authorisation boundary: requesting `rule_ids` the caller cannot see must silently omit them rather than erroring in a way that confirms their existence. The boundary is the #3488 rule (ownership and current grants, per frame and per snapshot row), not an intersection of ids with grants: grants alone must never deliver another user's rule (E35 threat model RE-E2, RE-S5, RE-I2).

## Accessibility notes
Backend, but it supplies SCR-087's content. The API must return condition values as structured nested rows so the screen can render "condition values in a nested table so a screen reader can read exactly why it fired" (SCR-087 a11y note), and every suppression reason needs a plain-language string agreed in E35-D03 rather than a raw enum token.

## Performance notes
SCR-087 requires 10k rows to scroll within 8 ms scripting per frame, which depends on cursor pagination and the `ix_rr_rule_time` / `ix_rr_matched` partial indexes rather than offset paging. WS `rules` coalesces at 250 ms per `23-ws-protocol.md` §8.2. Log writing must add <=1 ms to an evaluation at p99, measured.

## Observability
This story *is* observability, and additionally emits: `rule_log_rows_written_total{table}`, `rule_log_dropped_total`, `rule_log_queue_depth`, `rule_ws_subscribers`. Audit event `rule.fired {ruleId, version, trigger, metricSnapshot, actions, results, environment}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage: rule-engine package >=90% line (R3 local policy, roadmap §7.4), other backend >=85%, frontend >=80%; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated where behaviour diverged: `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11, `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4; ADR-0007 amended if an IR semantic changed.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit) and SCA (pip-audit/npm audit) clean or triaged with accepted-risk sign-off.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] PR(s) <=400 LOC diff, merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`rules_global_enabled`; `rules.graph_editor` where relevant).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E35-S03** (it logs what the executor did) and **#3488** (the `rules` topic's reading rule, `23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6, and the hub's `viewer` seam it delivers against; lands first). Uses tables from **E35-T02** and the WS infrastructure from **E05**/**E08**. Blocks **E35-S07** and **E35-S09**.

title: Detect rule conflicts at arming time and arbitrate deterministically at runtime
body:
## Context
US-RULE-011 exists because two armed rules touching the same position is not an exotic case — "move SL to breakeven at 1R" and "trail by ATR" are both reasonable and both want the stop. Without explicit precedence the outcome depends on evaluation order, which is exactly the kind of non-determinism this epic is built to eliminate. Its NFR: "arbitration is deterministic and covered by unit tests for every action pair."

The third scenario is a safety rule that overrides user configuration entirely: **a risk-control rule (daily loss, kill-switch, dead man's switch) always wins, regardless of configured priority**. A user must not be able to prioritise a discretionary rule above a risk control.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Arm-time conflict detection**: when a rule is armed (and on every save of an armed rule's new active version), compute the overlap set — rules whose resolved scopes intersect and whose actions target the same entity class (the same stop, the same position, overlapping flatten, opposing entries). Return the overlap matrix that SCR-086 renders, with conflict kinds `opposing_actions`, `duplicate_stop`, `overlapping_flatten`, `priority_ambiguity`.
- **Explicit precedence**: arming is blocked until the user sets a unique priority ordering within the overlap set (`rules.priority`, 0-1000, lower runs first per the DB comment). Ties within an overlap set are rejected, not silently broken.
- **Runtime arbitration**: when conflicting rules fire in the same evaluation tick, the higher-priority action is applied and the other is logged as `superseded`, with both visible in the firing log.
- **Safety override**: any action originating from a risk-control rule — the built-in `sys.*` rules, the daily-loss lockout, the dead man's switch, the kill-switch — wins over any discretionary rule irrespective of configured priority, and the override is logged.
- `rule.conflict_detected {ruleIds, scope, kind}`, `rule.conflict_resolved {choice}` and `rule.priority_changed` audit events.
- An "arm anyway" path that exists but requires an explicit acknowledgement (SCR-086 sign-off checklist), recorded in the audit trail.

## Out of scope
- The conflict resolver modal (SCR-086) — **E35-S09**.
- The risk-control rules themselves (daily loss, dead man's switch, kill-switch) — **E39**; the built-in `sys.*` rule definitions — **E35-T05**. This story classifies them and enforces their precedence.
- Cross-account conflict semantics beyond scope intersection — a fan-out concern owned by **E34**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Conflict is detected before both rules can be armed
  Given two armed-candidate rules that would both modify the same stop on the same position
  When the second is armed
  Then the conflict is detected at arming time and an explicit priority order must be set before both can stay armed

Scenario: Runtime arbitration is deterministic
  Given two conflicting rules that fire in the same evaluation tick
  When arbitration runs
  Then the higher-priority action is applied, the other is logged as superseded, and both are visible in the firing log

Scenario: Risk controls always win (failure case)
  Given a risk-control rule and a discretionary rule in conflict
  And the user has configured the discretionary rule at a higher priority
  When both fire
  Then the risk control is applied regardless of the configured priority, and the override is logged with its reason

Scenario: Ties are refused, not guessed (edge case)
  Given two rules in one overlap set assigned the same priority
  When arming is attempted
  Then it is rejected with an error naming both rules, and the tie is logged

Scenario: Arming anyway is possible but explicit
  Given a detected conflict the user judges acceptable
  When they choose to arm anyway
  Then an explicit acknowledgement is required and the decision is audited with both rule ids
```

## Technical notes / design
Overlap computation is a pairwise intersection over (resolved accounts x resolved symbols x `applies_to`) crossed with an **action-class** table that maps each of the 25 action types to the entity it mutates (`stop`, `take_profit`, `position_size`, `pending_orders`, `leverage`, `trading_enabled`, `none`). Two actions conflict when they mutate the same entity class on an intersecting scope. The table is the crux: it must be exhaustive, and the NFR's "unit tests for every action pair" is satisfied by a generated matrix test over the table, not by hand-written pairs.

Risk-control classification is a property of the rule, not of its priority: built-in `sys.*` rules and any rule whose actions include `halt_new_orders`, `flatten_all_positions` under the lockout policy, or that is flagged as a risk control by E39, sort into a separate precedence band that always precedes the discretionary band. Implement it as a two-level sort key (`band`, `priority`) so it cannot be defeated by a priority value.

Detection runs server-side at arm time **and** on rule save (SCR-086 performance note: results return in <=1 s for 500 rules), so the result must be computed from indexed, already-resolved scopes rather than by loading and compiling every rule.

## Test plan
Unit (>=90%): the generated action-pair matrix asserting the conflict verdict for every ordered pair of action classes; scope intersection across all `level`/`applies_to` combinations; two-band sort key including the attempted-defeat case (discretionary rule at priority 0 versus risk control at 1000); tie rejection.
Integration: arming flow blocked until priorities are unique; arbitration over a live tick where both rules match; superseded logging appearing in both runs' events.
Perf: detection over a seeded 500-rule dataset within the 1 s budget.
Contract: the conflict payload shape consumed by SCR-086.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

Specific to this ticket: precedence is a safety control. The two-band design exists so no user configuration — and no compromised or careless account — can rank a discretionary rule above a risk control; a test must attempt exactly that and fail the build if it succeeds. The "arm anyway" escape hatch is audited with both rule ids and the acknowledging actor, because it is the point where a human accepts a known-conflicting configuration.

## Accessibility notes
Backend, but SCR-086 requires conflicts to be presented as a table (rule A, rule B, overlapping scope, conflicting actions, proposed resolution) with each proposed resolution a labelled radio stating its consequence in text. The API must therefore return each conflict as structured fields plus a plain-language consequence string per resolution option, not a rendered sentence.

## Performance notes
Conflict detection <=1 s for 500 rules at arm time and on save (SCR-086). Runtime arbitration must be O(conflicting rules) within the evaluation tick and must not add measurably to the evaluation budget.

## Observability
`rule_conflicts_detected_total{kind}`, `rule_actions_superseded_total`, `rule_safety_override_total`, `rule_conflict_detection_duration_seconds`. Audit: `rule.conflict_detected`, `rule.conflict_resolved`, `rule.priority_changed`, and the arm-anyway acknowledgement.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage: rule-engine package >=90% line (R3 local policy, roadmap §7.4), other backend >=85%, frontend >=80%; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated where behaviour diverged: `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11, `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4; ADR-0007 amended if an IR semantic changed.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit) and SCA (pip-audit/npm audit) clean or triaged with accepted-risk sign-off.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] PR(s) <=400 LOC diff, merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`rules_global_enabled`; `rules.graph_editor` where relevant).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E35-S06** (superseded actions are logged through it). Classifies risk-control rules supplied by **E39** and the built-ins from **E35-T05**. Blocks **E35-S09** (the resolver UI).

## Branch
`feat/rule-engine-conflict-precedence`, ~250 LOC plus the generated matrix test.

- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0007-rule-ir.md` — one canonical IR, binding rules 1-8
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4 — `rules`, `rule_versions`, `rule_runs`, `rule_events`
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` — `/rules`, `/rules/{ruleId}`, `/rules/{ruleId}/versions`, `/rules/{ruleId}/active-version`, `/rules/validate`, `/rules/{ruleId}/compile`, `/rules/{ruleId}/simulate`, `/rules/{ruleId}/mode`, `/rules/{ruleId}/runs`, `/rules/runs/{runId}/events`, `/rules/vocabulary`
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6 `RuleUpdate` — topic `rules`, options `rule_ids`/`include_events`, 250 ms cadence
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §20 RULE (US-RULE-001..011)

title: Build the rule simulation panel and the rule arming dialog
body:
## Context
These two screens are the human gate between "a rule I wrote" and "a rule that trades". SCR-084 is the evidence and SCR-085 is the decision, and the product deliberately couples them: a rule cannot be armed without a completed simulation on its exact `ir_hash` (E35-S01, `22-api-openapi.yaml` arming preconditions), and `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.7's new-rule gate makes simulate the mandatory on-ramp.

Both screens carry copy requirements that are part of the specification rather than decoration. SCR-084: "Simulation replays recorded market data. Fills are modelled, not real; results are not a guarantee." SCR-085: "If the backend stops, this rule stops. Native stops stay." Those sentences manage risk R12 (backtest bias) and the user's mental model of what automation guarantees; they ship verbatim.

Design must be Status=Done for >=2 sprints before this story starts (design-ahead rule), which is why E35-D02/D05 sit in S15 and S16.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-084 Rule simulation / backtest panel** (page section or drawer from either editor): range, symbol and account selectors; the available-history statement rendered from the API's true coverage ("history available: 13 of 14 days (recording started 09-01)"); run with progress and cancel; result summary (fires, actions by type, errors); the per-firing timeline with the triggering context; "open in chart at this moment" deep link; CSV export.
  States: idle, running (cancellable), completed, **partial** (history gaps listed explicitly with the missing windows), failed, **no-history** (CTA to record the symbol).
- **SCR-085 Rule arming dialog** (modal): environment radio group with **DEMO preselected**; scope confirmation expanding a trade group into an explicit account list; the safety summary (does it place orders? can it flatten? does it depend on estimated detectors?); engine-availability note; conflict warning linking to SCR-086 when another armed rule targets the same scope; typed confirmation plus step-up 2FA for LIVE; the disarm path.
  Validation: cannot arm a failing-validation rule; cannot arm live on an account the user cannot trade; `flatten_all_positions` needs an extra acknowledgement.
- **Components**: CMP-154 RuleSimulatePanel, CMP-023 Progress Bar, CMP-026 EmptyState, CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-047 DateRangePicker, CMP-049 Table, CMP-167 JournalEquityCurveChart, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-044 ConfirmDialog, CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger, CMP-158 SafetyInvariantNotice, CMP-159 RuleConflictWarning, CMP-233 RuleOptions.
- **Data**: `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/simulate`, progress on WS `rules`, results via `GET /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/runs`; `PUT /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/mode` with the step-up token.
- Analytics/audit emission: `rule.simulation_started|completed|cancelled`, `rule.armed`.

## Out of scope
- The editors that host the panel (SCR-081/082) — E36/E37; this story ships the panel as a mountable surface with a route-level demo host.
- The conflict resolver modal (SCR-086) — **E35-S09**; this story only links to it.
- Step-up MFA mechanics — **E09**; this story invokes it.
- The chart deep link's target rendering — E11/E26.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Simulation reports coverage honestly
  Given a requested 14-day range where recording covers 13 days
  When the simulation completes
  Then the panel shows the partial state naming the missing window explicitly
  And the required caveat copy about modelled fills is visible without interaction

Scenario: No recorded history offers the fix (failure case)
  Given a symbol that has never been recorded
  When a simulation is requested
  Then the no-history state is shown with a call to action to start recording the symbol, not an empty result table

Scenario: Arming live demands deliberate confirmation
  Given a rule scoped to an account the user may trade live
  When the arming dialog opens
  Then DEMO is preselected, the accounts and symbols are restated explicitly, and arming LIVE requires typing the confirmation and a step-up 2FA code

Scenario: Armed state is never optimistic (edge case)
  Given the user confirms arming
  When the API responds but the rules WS confirmation has not yet arrived
  Then the dialog stays open in a pending state and closes only once the armed state is confirmed over the rules topic

Scenario: A rule that cannot be armed says why (failure case)
  Given a rule with open safety-class validation warnings or no simulation on its current version
  When the arming dialog opens
  Then the arm action is disabled with a visible reason naming the missing precondition and what to do about it

Scenario: Keyboard-only arming
  Given a user operating without a pointer
  When they open the arming dialog
  Then focus moves into the dialog, the environment radio group is reachable and operable, the typed confirmation and 2FA fields have visible labels,
  And Escape cancels without arming
```

## Technical notes / design
Both surfaces are thin over the API — resist re-deriving anything. Specifically: coverage text, the safety summary (does it place orders / can it flatten / estimated-detector dependency) and the arming preconditions all come from the server, because a client-side re-derivation would eventually disagree with what the server enforces, and the disagreement would appear precisely at the moment a user is deciding to risk money.

Simulation progress arrives on the WS `rules` topic at its 250 ms cadence; the UI must stay fully interactive during a run (SCR-084 performance note) — run result parsing off the main thread if a large timeline arrives.

The arming dialog is `role="alertdialog"`. The typed confirmation uses CMP-044 ConfirmDialog's `variant="typed"` pattern already established for dangerous actions (CMP-145 uses the same pattern for live-arming from the form editor).

Never close the dialog on the HTTP 200 alone — SCR-085 is explicit that the armed state is confirmed over `rules` before the dialog closes.

## Test plan
Unit/component (>=80% frontend): every enumerated state of both screens rendered from fixtures — idle, running, completed, partial, failed, no-history for SCR-084; default, live-selected, blocked-by-precondition, conflict-warning, engine-offline and disarm for SCR-085.
Interaction: cancel a running simulation; progress updates from a mocked WS; pending-until-WS-confirmation arming; Escape cancels.
a11y: axe-core on both screens in every state; keyboard-only traversal test; screen-reader label assertions on the radio group, typed field and 2FA field.
E2E (Playwright, extended in **E35-Q03**): simulate a rule over a recorded window then arm it on demo, asserting the audit events were emitted.
Visual regression on the two screens' primary states.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

Specific to this ticket: arming is a privileged, audited action and the UI must not become a way around the server's checks. The arm control being disabled is a courtesy — every precondition is enforced server-side (E35-S01), and a test crafting the API call directly must still be refused. The step-up 2FA token is passed through, never cached in component state beyond the request. The environment radio defaulting to DEMO is a safety control, not a convenience default, and needs an explicit test. Simulation results are evidence for arming, so their audit events are emitted by the server, not trusted from the client.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-084: results are a table, and the firing timeline has a text-list equivalent; progress is announced through a live region rather than by the visual bar alone; the caveat copy is in the reading order, not a tooltip.
SCR-085: `role="alertdialog"`; the rule's behaviour is restated in plain language; the environment choice is a radio group with DEMO preselected; the typed confirmation field has a visible label and a format hint; focus is trapped and returns to the trigger on close; the conflict warning is announced.
Both: WCAG 2.2 AA contrast on every status treatment, and no state distinguished by colour alone (armed/disarmed/error are text plus icon).

## Performance notes
SCR-084: the UI stays fully interactive during a run; partial results stream in rather than arriving as one blocking payload; a 14-day run's timeline renders without blocking input. SCR-085: arming takes effect server-side within 1 s including the WS confirmation the dialog waits for.

## Observability
Client analytics: `rule.simulation_started|completed|cancelled` and `rule.armed` are emitted server-side; the client emits the UI-only events for funnel analysis. Client errors on the arming path are reported with the rule id and precondition code so a stuck user is diagnosable.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage: rule-engine package >=90% line (R3 local policy, roadmap §7.4), other backend >=85%, frontend >=80%; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated where behaviour diverged: `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11, `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4; ADR-0007 amended if an IR semantic changed.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit) and SCA (pip-audit/npm audit) clean or triaged with accepted-risk sign-off.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] PR(s) <=400 LOC diff, merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`rules_global_enabled`; `rules.graph_editor` where relevant).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on the touched screens; manual screen-reader pass (NVDA or VoiceOver) recorded; keyboard-only path verified against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- [ ] design-qa: built screens compared against the signed-off Figma spec (spacing, tokens, type, colour, every enumerated state) by a designer; discrepancies fixed or filed as Bugs with `priority/*`.
- [ ] Storybook entries added under `RuleEngine/*` for every new or changed component, covering each state including empty, loading, error and the degraded/engine-offline variants.
