title: Build the fire history, IR inspector, conflict resolver and import/export UI
body:
## Context
Four smaller surfaces that together make the rule engine explainable, portable and safe to operate:
- **SCR-087 Rule fire history** answers "why did / didn't my rule fire" — US-RULE-010's whole purpose.
- **SCR-088 Rule IR inspector** shows the canonical IR read-only plus the compiled evaluation plan, and is the surface that makes the round-trip guarantee visible to a human ("used for debugging, support and for verifying form↔graph round-trip equivalence").
- **SCR-086 Rule conflict resolver** forces an explicit precedence ordering before two overlapping rules can both stay armed — US-RULE-011.
- **SCR-089 Rule import / export** moves rules between installations, with two hard rules from the sign-off checklist: "the exported bundle never contains account ids, keys or armed state" and "imported rules always land disarmed", both **stated and verified**.

Design must be Done >=2 sprints before this story starts (E35-D03/D05).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-087** (page/drawer): virtualised, cursor-paginated table over `GET /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/runs` with live append from WS `rules`; columns time, rule version, trigger, metric snapshot, actions attempted, results, environment; failure rows highlighted with the exchange reason; engine-restart markers; filters by outcome and environment; link from a firing to the resulting order and audit record; "replay this moment" link; export. States: empty, streaming, failure-highlighted, engine-restart markers.
- **SCR-088** (drawer) — **E35-D03's deltas only**, onto the base IR-inspector screen E36-S03 (#1059) builds (design boundary, E35-D05 §11 / ruling 6463770354 BQ-29): the CMP-240 tree content with masking (`SCR-088/masked-pre`), Download diff (JSON) on the round-trip diff view (`SCR-088/mismatch-download`) and the graph-node inset on the compile-failure state (`SCR-088/issues-graph-anchor`), as `docs/design/E35/E35-D03.md` §7 (SCR-088) and the E35-D05 pack §11 list them. The read-only canonical IR with its copy control, the diff view itself, the version and compiler-version stamps, the advanced/diagnostic pill, the compile-failure state's base clauses and the worker-side highlighting are E36-S03's base — checked here on the integrated screen, never built twice.
- **SCR-086** (modal): the overlap matrix as a table (rule A, rule B, overlapping scope, conflicting actions, proposed resolution); conflict kinds (opposing actions, duplicate stops, overlapping flatten, priority ambiguity); resolution choices (set priority, narrow scope, disarm one) each stating its consequence; "arm anyway" behind an explicit acknowledgement; the no-conflict state.
- **SCR-089** (modal) — **E35-D03's deltas only**, onto the base import/export screen E36-S06 (#1062) builds (design boundary, E35-D05 §11 BQ-29): the export verification strip computed from the returned bundle (`SCR-089/export-verified`), the import pre-check checkbox column (`SCR-089/import-precheck-controls`), the version-mismatch rows (`SCR-089/import-mismatch`: the format and the IR-version rows), the import-results landing word per row (`SCR-089/import-results-landing`: DRAFT · not armed · on DEMO) and CMP-234 as the validation-failure host (`SCR-089/validation-panel`, entries move focus to the row). The export selection (single / selected / all) with the scope-stripping note, the import preview with per-rule accept/skip and the validation failure list naming the rule and the field are E36-S06's base — checked here on the integrated screen.
- **Components**: CMP-036 KeyValueRow, CMP-047 DateRangePicker, CMP-049 Table, CMP-055 FilterBar, CMP-156 RuleEvaluationTimeline, CMP-033 CopyButton, CMP-046 Drawer, CMP-068 CopyableCodeBlock, CMP-234 ValidationPanel, CMP-001 Button, CMP-006 RadioGroup, CMP-155 RuleListRow, CMP-159 RuleConflictWarning, CMP-027 ErrorState/InlineError, CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-067 FileDrop.
- **Data**: `GET /api/v1/rules/runs/{runId}/events`, `GET /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/runs`, `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/compile`, WS `rules`.

## Out of scope
- The rules list SCR-080 that hosts the conflict banner — E36; this story ships the modal it links to.
- The audit-log browser — **E42**.
- Replay playback itself — **E26**; this story only deep-links into it.
- Import of workspaces or layouts (US-LAY-007) — E17; only rule bundles here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A firing explains itself
  Given a rule fired and moved a stop
  When the user opens that row in the fire history
  Then the condition values that produced the decision are shown as a nested table, alongside the actions attempted and the resulting order ids

Scenario: A suppressed firing is visible too
  Given a rule that would have fired but was suppressed by a cooldown
  When the history is filtered by outcome
  Then the suppressed evaluation appears with its specific reason in words

Scenario: The IR inspector proves the round trip
  Given a rule authored in one editor and opened in the other
  When the inspector is opened
  Then the canonical IR, its hash, the version and the compiler version are shown read-only, and the round-trip diff view is empty for a matching pair

Scenario: Compilation failure names the offender (failure case)
  Given a rule whose compilation fails
  When the inspector is opened
  Then an error state names the offending node or row rather than showing an empty document

Scenario: Conflicts cannot be ignored silently
  Given two armed-candidate rules targeting the same stop
  When the resolver opens
  Then each resolution option states its consequence in text, and arming anyway requires an explicit acknowledgement

Scenario: Exported rules carry no secrets and import disarmed (failure case)
  Given a rule bound to two accounts and currently armed
  When it is exported and then imported into another installation
  Then the bundle contains no account ids, keys or armed state, the import preview shows how references are remapped
  And the imported rule lands disarmed
```

## Technical notes / design
SCR-087 is the performance-sensitive one: a virtualised table over cursor pagination with live append from the WS, budgeted at 10k rows without exceeding 8 ms scripting per frame. Live rows append at the top without disturbing the user's scroll position or stealing focus — a log that jumps while being read is worse than no log.

SCR-088's diff view renders the structured diff the server produced (E35-T04); the client does not compute a diff, because a client-side diff of two canonical documents could disagree with the server's verdict on whether a round trip succeeded.

SCR-089's guarantees are enforced server-side — the client displays them. The import preview is rendered from the server's per-rule accept/skip decision including its reason; "unknown metric or action names are rejected with the offending path named" (SCR-089 validation note).

All four surfaces must handle the engine-offline state coherently: SCR-080's banner copy ("The rule engine is not running — armed rules are not evaluating. Native stops are unaffected.") sets the tone — always say what is still protecting the user.

## Test plan
Unit/component (>=80%): each screen in every enumerated state from fixtures; virtualised table with 10k rows; live append preserving scroll and focus; worker-based highlighting above 100 KB; import preview with accept, skip and version-mismatch rows.
a11y: axe-core on all four screens in every state; the nested condition-value table read correctly by a screen reader; the IR inspector's structured tree alternative navigable by keyboard; the resolver's radio options announced with their consequences.
E2E (extended in **E35-Q03**): fire a rule on demo, open its history row, inspect its IR, export it, re-import it and assert it is disarmed.
Perf: the SCR-087 scripting budget measured under the 10k-row fixture.
Visual regression on the primary state of each screen.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

Specific to this ticket: export is a data-exfiltration surface. The bundle must never contain account ids, API keys, armed state or any `rule_runs.input_snapshot` content; this is verified by a test that exports a fully-populated rule and asserts the serialised bundle against a deny-list of field names. Import is an injection surface: the server validates and compiles every imported document, remaps references to what the importing user can access, and lands the rule disarmed — the client must never construct a rule locally and POST it as pre-validated. `rule.imported`/`rule.exported` are audited. The fire history exposes financial data and is gated by `rules:read` with account scoping.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-087: condition values in a nested table so a screen reader can read exactly why a rule fired; filters keyboard-operable; live-appended rows announced politely, never assertively, and never moving focus.
SCR-088: the `<pre>` region has a described-by note explaining it is read-only canonical JSON; a copy button is provided; a structured expandable tree alternative is offered for screen-reader navigation.
SCR-086: conflicts are a table; each proposed resolution is a labelled radio with its consequence in text.
SCR-089: export and import are separate labelled sections; the import diff is a table; every validation failure names the rule and the field.

## Performance notes
SCR-087: 10k rows scroll within 8 ms scripting per frame; history is cursor-paginated, never offset-paginated. SCR-088: IR fetched on demand; highlighting in a worker above 100 KB. SCR-086: conflict detection returns within 1 s for 500 rules (server-side, E35-S07). SCR-089: a 100-rule bundle validates in <=2 s with per-rule results streamed.

## Observability
Client analytics: `rule.history_viewed`, `rule.history_exported`, `rule.fire_detail_opened`, `rule.ir_viewed`, `rule.ir_copied`, `rule.template_previewed`. Server-side audits `rule.imported`, `rule.exported`, `rule.conflict_resolved`, `rule.priority_changed` are emitted by the API, not the client.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage: rule-engine package >=90% line (R3 local policy, roadmap §7.4), other backend >=85%, frontend >=80%; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated where behaviour diverged: `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11, `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4; ADR-0007 amended if an IR semantic changed.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit) and SCA (pip-audit/npm audit) clean or triaged with accepted-risk sign-off.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] PR(s) <=400 LOC diff, merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`rules_global_enabled`; `rules.graph_editor` where relevant).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on the touched screens; manual screen-reader pass (NVDA or VoiceOver) recorded; keyboard-only path verified against `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- [ ] design-qa: built screens compared against the signed-off Figma spec (spacing, tokens, type, colour, every enumerated state) by a designer; discrepancies fixed or filed as Bugs with `priority/*`.
- [ ] Storybook entries added under `RuleEngine/*` for every new or changed component, covering each state including empty, loading, error and the degraded/engine-offline variants.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E35-S06** (runs and events APIs, WS `rules`), **E35-S07** (conflict payload), **E35-D05** (handoff Done >=2 sprints earlier) and, for the SCR-088 / SCR-089 base screens this story builds its deltas onto, **E36-S03** and **E36-S06** (E35-D05 §11 BQ-29). Blocks **E35-T06** and **E35-Q06**.

## Branch
`feat/rule-engine-diagnostics-ui`. Three or four PRs, one per screen, to stay inside the 400-LOC guidance.

## References

title: Implement the rule IR models, canonical serialisation and content hash
body:
## Context
This is the foundation stone of E35 and of E36/E37: the single typed representation every rule reduces to. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11.2 gives the complete pydantic model set (`Rule`, `RuleScope`, `Trigger`, `MetricRef`, `Comparison`, `ArithmeticNode`, `BooleanNode`, `TemporalNode`, `Action`, `RuleLimits`) and §11.3 gives the JSON Schema those models must generate. ADR-0007 fixes the binding rules.

Nothing downstream can start without this: the validator (T04), the evaluator (S02), both editors (E36/E37) and the alerts grammar (E40) all target it. It is therefore scheduled first in S14 and merges as its own PR ahead of consumers, per the interface-first rule in `docs/plan/01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10.

## Scope / Deliverables
- New package `packages/rule_ir/` (pure, dependency-light, no I/O, no DB, no network) containing:
  - Every pydantic v2 model in `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.2, field-for-field, including the discriminated `ConditionNode` union and the `Operand` union.
  - `canonicalize(ir) -> bytes` and `ir_hash(ir) -> str` implementing the strategy chosen in **ADR-0016** (E35-K01): sorted keys, normalised numbers, `node_id` handling per the ADR, `graph_layout`/`form_model`/presentation fields excluded.
  - `to_json_schema()` emitting the document published at `GET /api/v1/schemas/rule-ir.json` (`24-internal-schemas.md` §11.3 / §17.3), generated at build time rather than hand-maintained.
  - `form_compatible(ir) -> bool` plus `form_incompatibility_reasons(ir)`, implementing the **form subset** definition in §11.4: trigger + a two-level boolean tree (`all_of` of `any_of` of comparisons) + a flat action list + limits; arithmetic operands only as a parameterised metric (no nested arithmetic); temporal nodes only as `sustained_for` directly wrapping a comparison. This is what lets E36 render a graph-authored rule read-only instead of mangling it.
- A CI check that fails if the committed `rule-ir.json` differs from the generated one (schema drift guard).
- Promote the E35-K01 corpus into `tests/fixtures/rule_ir/` and grow it toward the >=30-rule corpus required by R3 exit criterion 5.
- Publish the package build so the TypeScript side can consume the generated JSON Schema for editor-side pre-validation (E36/E37 consume, do not re-derive).

## Out of scope
- Semantic validation (metric existence, type/unit compatibility, action parameter completeness) — **E35-T04**. This package does structural typing only.
- Persistence — **E35-T02**. No SQLAlchemy models here.
- Evaluation — **E35-S02**.
- IR version upcasters — **E35-T05** (the `ir_version` field exists here; migration functions do not).
- Any TypeScript reimplementation of canonicalisation: the canonical hash is computed server-side only, a constraint recorded in ADR-0016.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Canonical hash is stable under cosmetic difference
  Given two IR documents identical except for key insertion order, numeric formatting (1.50 vs 1.5) and graph_layout node coordinates
  When both are canonicalised and hashed
  Then the two ir_hash values are equal

Scenario: Presentation fields are excluded from the hash
  Given an IR document with hand-placed node positions and comment text
  When only those presentation fields change
  Then ir_hash is unchanged, and the presentation block is returned untouched by round-tripping the models

Scenario: Form-subset detection is honest (edge case)
  Given a graph rule whose output fans one node into two consumers, or that nests arithmetic inside arithmetic
  When form_compatible is called
  Then it returns false and form_incompatibility_reasons names the offending node_id and the specific construct

Scenario: Structurally invalid document is rejected loudly (failure case)
  Given a document with an unknown action type, a boolean node with 33 children, or a temporal node missing window_ms
  When it is parsed
  Then a ValidationError is raised naming the failing JSON path, and no partially-constructed Rule object is returned

Scenario: Schema drift is caught in CI
  Given a developer edits a pydantic model without regenerating rule-ir.json
  When CI runs
  Then the schema-drift check fails with a diff of the two documents
```

## Technical notes / design
Implement the models exactly as printed in `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.2 — treat that section as the specification, and if implementation forces a deviation, the doc changes in the same PR (DoD requirement), it is not silently diverged from.

Key details that are easy to get wrong:
- `ConditionNode = Comparison | BooleanNode | TemporalNode` must be a **discriminated** union on `op` so error messages point at the right branch rather than producing a three-way union error dump.
- `Operand = MetricRef | Literal_ | ArithmeticNode` — the literal wrapper is `{"const": ...}` in JSON per §11.3 `$defs.operand`.
- `MetricRef.metric` is constrained by `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,48}$`; symbols by `^[A-Z0-9]{4,20}$`.
- Trigger conditionals from §11.3 (`on_timer` requires `interval_ms`, `on_bar_close` requires `timeframe`, `on_schedule` requires `cron`, `on_metric_change` requires `metric`) are model validators *and* JSON Schema `allOf/if/then` — both representations must agree, asserted by a test.
- `RuleScope.environments` defaults to `("demo",)`. This safe default is a safety control (§11.5 E12), not a convenience; a test asserts the default explicitly so a future refactor cannot quietly widen it.
- `RuleLimits` defaults must match §11.2 exactly: `cooldown_ms=1000`, `max_fires_per_hour=60`, `max_fires_per_day=500`, `max_actions_per_fire=10`, `evaluation_timeout_ms=250`, `kill_switch_on_error_count=5`.
- Hash **before** persistence; never recompute from a Postgres `jsonb` round-trip, which reorders keys (ADR-0016).

## Test plan
Unit (target >=95% on this package — it is the smallest and most consequential):
- Parse/serialise round trip for every fixture in `tests/fixtures/rule_ir/`.
- Hash stability under key reorder, number reformatting, layout change, comment change.
- Hash *inequality* under any semantic change (threshold, operator, action order, scope, limits) — a table-driven test over one mutation per field.
- `form_compatible` truth table over the subset definition, one case per disqualifying construct.
- Trigger conditional validators, one case per trigger type, valid and invalid.
- Bound violations: 33 boolean children, 9 arithmetic operands, 11 actions, `window_ms` below 100 and above 86 400 000.
Property-based (Hypothesis, strategy from ADR-0016): generate valid IR, assert `parse(serialise(x)) == x` and hash stability; this suite is grown to the 10 000-documents-per-CI-run NFR by **E35-Q02**.
Contract: generated `rule-ir.json` validates every fixture with an independent JSON Schema validator (`jsonschema`), proving the pydantic models and the published schema agree.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

Specific to this ticket: `additionalProperties: false` throughout the schema is a security control — it stops an attacker or a buggy editor smuggling unrecognised fields into a stored IR that a later engine version might interpret. title: Add the rules, rule_versions, rule_runs and rule_events migration with retention
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4 specifies the rule-engine relational schema in full DDL. This ticket lands it as an Alembic migration with the retention policy attached, because the retention decision is not cosmetic: a 250 ms evaluator produces roughly **345 000 rows per day per rule** if every evaluation is persisted, so the schema doc mandates that a `rule_runs` row is written only when `matched = true`, when `status = 'error'`, or when the rule is in `simulate` mode with the per-rule `record_all` flag set. Non-persisted evaluations are counted in Prometheus only.

The append-only guarantee on `rule_events` is a non-repudiation control (the firing log is part of the audit trail per US-RULE-010's NFR: "log retained indefinitely — it is part of the audit trail").

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration creating enums `rule_scope`, `rule_mode`, `rule_run_status` and tables `rules`, `rule_versions`, `rule_runs`, `rule_events` exactly as specified in `21-database-schema.md` §3.4.1–§3.4.3, including every CHECK constraint (`rule_editor`, `rule_interval`, `rule_cooldown`, `rule_prio`, `rule_scope_acct`, `rule_scope_sym`, `rule_armed_shape`, `rule_fires_pos`, `rv_version_pos`, `rv_ir_obj`, `rr_trigger`, `rr_duration`, `re_kind`), every index (`ux_rules_name`, `ix_rules_active`, `ix_rules_symbol`, `ix_rules_account`, `ix_rv_rule`, `ix_rr_rule_time`, `ix_rr_matched`, `ix_rr_errors`, `ix_rr_group`, `ix_re_run`, `ix_re_time`), the deferred FK `rules_active_version_fk`, and the uniqueness pair `UNIQUE (rule_id, version)` / `UNIQUE (rule_id, ir_hash)`.
- The `trg_re_append` trigger on `rule_events` calling `forbid_mutation()` (the shared function already used by `audit_log`, `order_events`, `executions`, `alert_deliveries` per §1).
- SQLAlchemy models and a repository module mapping `rule_versions.ir` (jsonb) to the `packages/rule_ir` models from E35-T01, hashing **before** insert.
- Retention job registration per §7: prune non-matched `rule_runs` (and their cascading `rule_events`) after 7 days; keep matched runs 24 months then archive to Parquet. The job is scheduled but its Parquet writer reuses the existing cold-storage path (E03/E16), it is not rebuilt here.
- A downgrade path that is tested, not merely written.

## Out of scope
- API handlers over these tables — **E35-S01**.
- The `alerts` table, which shares the IR grammar — **E40**.
- `trade_groups.origin_rule_id` / `origin_rule_run_id` columns — owned by **E34**; this migration must simply not conflict with them (ordering handled by Alembic branch labels).
- Parquet archive writer internals — E16.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Migration applies and reverses cleanly
  Given an empty database at the previous revision
  When the migration is applied and then downgraded
  Then both directions succeed with no residual objects and the test suite for the prior revision still passes

Scenario: An armed rule must be fully specified (failure case)
  Given an UPDATE setting rules.mode = 'armed' without armed_at, armed_by or active_version_id
  When the statement executes
  Then the rule_armed_shape CHECK rejects it

Scenario: Saving an unchanged rule creates no new version (edge case)
  Given a rule whose stored version already has ir_hash H
  When a save produces the same canonical IR and therefore the same H
  Then the UNIQUE (rule_id, ir_hash) constraint prevents a duplicate version row and the repository returns the existing version

Scenario: Rule events cannot be altered (failure case)
  Given a persisted rule_events row
  When an UPDATE or DELETE is attempted by any role including the application role
  Then trg_re_append raises and the row is unchanged

Scenario: Retention prunes noise but keeps evidence
  Given 8-day-old non-matched runs and 8-day-old matched runs
  When the retention job runs
  Then only the non-matched runs and their events are deleted, and the matched runs remain
```

## Technical notes / design
Copy the DDL verbatim from `21-database-schema.md` §3.4 — deviations are bugs, not improvements. Notes:
- `rules.active_version_id` FK is added **after** `rule_versions` exists (the doc shows the `ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT` ordering); with `ON DELETE RESTRICT` so an executing version cannot be deleted out from under the engine.
- `rv_ir_obj` (`jsonb_typeof(ir) = 'object' AND ir ? 'conditions' AND ir ? 'actions'`) is a cheap last-line structural guard; it does not replace schema validation in the application.
- `ix_rr_matched` and `ix_rr_errors` are partial indexes — they are what keeps SCR-087's history query fast while the table stays mostly write-only.
- The per-rule `record_all` flag lives in the `settings` table under `rules.settings.record_all` per §3.4.3, not as a column on `rules`.
- The repository must never recompute `ir_hash` from the jsonb column after a read, because Postgres reorders jsonb keys; the stored hash is authoritative.
- Write the migration so it is safe to run against a database that already holds E34's `trade_groups`: use an explicit `depends_on` in the Alembic revision.

## Test plan
Unit/integration against a real Postgres 16 in testcontainers (not SQLite):
- Upgrade/downgrade idempotence.
- One test per CHECK constraint asserting the rejection, including the boundary values (`eval_interval_ms` 49/50/3600000/3600001, `cooldown_seconds` -1/0/86400/86401, `priority` -1/0/1000/1001).
- Unique-index behaviour: duplicate name for the same owner (case-insensitive, ignoring soft-deleted rows), duplicate `(rule_id, version)`, duplicate `(rule_id, ir_hash)`.
- Append-only trigger on UPDATE and DELETE.
- Cascade behaviour: deleting a `rules` row cascades to versions and runs; deleting a `rule_versions` row that is active is RESTRICTed.
- Retention job over a seeded time-spread dataset.
Coverage target >=85% on the repository module.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

Specific to this ticket: `rule_runs.input_snapshot` stores the metric values the conditions saw, which can include account equity, unrealised PnL and position size — classify as **financial/confidential**. It must be readable only through `rules:read` with account scoping, never dumped into general application logs. The append-only trigger on `rule_events` is the non-repudiation control; a migration that drops or weakens it is a security regression and must be blocked in review. Security review label required.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — database migration, no UI surface.

## Performance notes
Verify with `EXPLAIN` that SCR-087's history query (`rule_runs` by `rule_id` ordered by `started_at DESC`, cursor-paginated) uses `ix_rr_rule_time` and that the matched-only variant uses the partial `ix_rr_matched`. Insert throughput must sustain the worst-case matched-run write rate without lock contention on `rule_events`' bigserial.

## Observability
Add `rule_runs_persisted_total{reason}` (matched|error|record_all) and `rule_runs_pruned_total` so the write-amplification decision can be verified in production rather than assumed. Retention job emits a structured log with rows deleted and duration.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage: rule-engine package >=90% line (R3 local policy, roadmap §7.4), other backend >=85%, frontend >=80%; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated where behaviour diverged: `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11, `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4; ADR-0007 amended if an IR semantic changed.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit) and SCA (pip-audit/npm audit) clean or triaged with accepted-risk sign-off.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] PR(s) <=400 LOC diff, merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`rules_global_enabled`; `rules.graph_editor` where relevant).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E35-T01** (the repository maps to those models). Blocks **E35-S01**. Coordinates with **E34** on Alembic revision ordering for `trade_groups`.

## Branch
`feat/rule-engine-db-migration` — migration + models + repository, ~300 LOC.

title: Build the metric and action vocabulary registry and serve GET /rules/vocabulary
body:
## Context
US-RULE-002 (metric vocabulary) and US-RULE-003 (action vocabulary) require a documented, closed catalogue of everything a rule can react to and everything it can do. `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` describes `GET /api/v1/rules/vocabulary` as the single response **both** editors render their palettes from — "which is what keeps the two editors round-trip compatible". If the two editors ever derived their palettes independently, they would drift, and the round-trip guarantee would fail in the field rather than in CI.

Critically, `24-internal-schemas.md` §7 states the `MetricRegistry` is a *single named registry* shared by the rule engine, alerts, the journal and the UI: "This is what makes the rule vocabulary and the indicator list the same list." This ticket exposes that registry rather than duplicating it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A `vocabulary` module that projects the existing `MetricRegistry` (`24-internal-schemas.md` §7.2, populated by E12/E18/E19/E20/E23/E24/**E25**) into rule vocabulary entries carrying: stable `metric` name, human label, description, **unit** (price/ratio/percent/duration/count/enum), valid range, `warmup_bars`, `deterministic`, **`confidence`** (exact vs estimated), parameter schema, required data dependencies, and the behaviour when unavailable.
- The action catalogue: all 25 `Action.type` values from `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.2 with their per-type required/optional parameter JSON Schemas from §11.6, each declaring the permission it needs (`orders:write`, `rules.loosen_stop` for `only_tighten=false`, `rules.arm_live`), its target semantics (`scope_accounts`/`originating_account`/`all_accounts`), and whether it is idempotent or guarded.
- The trigger catalogue: the 13 trigger types with their required companion fields.
- The operator catalogue with type/unit compatibility rules (which operators apply to which unit classes; `in_set`/`not_in_set` only for enum-typed metrics).
- `GET /api/v1/rules/vocabulary` returning `RuleVocabulary` with `x-rbac: { permissions: [rules:read], scope: none }`, ETag-cacheable.
- `GET /api/v1/schemas/rule-ir.json` serving the generated document from E35-T01.
- Unavailability data: for a given symbol, which metrics are unusable because the symbol is not recorded, with the one-click "start recording" action reference the UI needs (US-RULE-002 scenario 2) — surfaced as a `requires_recording` dependency plus the recorder endpoint the UI should call.
- Every heuristic metric flagged `confidence: "estimated"` so the picker and the rule summary can badge it (US-RULE-002 scenario 3) — this is the product-wide *(estimated)* framing from the detector screens.

## Out of scope
- Implementing any metric — they come from E12/E18-E25. This ticket only projects and describes them.
- Rendering the palette — E36/E37.
- Executing actions — **E35-S03**.
- Validating a specific rule against the vocabulary — **E35-T04**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The documented catalogue is complete
  Given the vocabulary endpoint is called
  Then price, R-multiple, ATR, EMA/SMA, swing high/low, CVD and its divergences, delta, imbalance stacks, absorption, stop-run, iceberg flags,
       tape-speed z-score, book speed, regime, spread, funding rate and time-to-funding, OI change, position age, unrealised PnL,
       account equity and drawdown are each present with a unit and a description

Scenario: Estimated metrics are badged
  Given a metric whose registry descriptor has confidence other than exact
  When the vocabulary is returned
  Then that entry carries estimated: true so the picker and the rule summary can display the (estimated) badge

Scenario: Unavailable metric names its dependency (edge case)
  Given a symbol that is not in the recorded-symbol list
  When the vocabulary is requested scoped to that symbol
  Then metrics needing recorded data are returned disabled, each naming the missing dependency and the recorder action that would satisfy it

Scenario: Actions declare their permission (failure case)
  Given a user without orders:write on any account
  When the vocabulary is returned
  Then order-placing actions are present but marked as available in simulate mode only, with the restriction explained in text

Scenario: The registry is the single source (regression guard)
  Given a metric is added to the MetricRegistry without a vocabulary descriptor
  When CI runs
  Then the completeness test fails naming the metric, so the two lists cannot drift
```

## Technical notes / design
Metric identity must be **stable across versions** (US-RULE-002 NFR) — renaming a metric breaks every stored rule referencing it, so renames go through the IR migration path (E35-T05), never a silent change. Enforce with a golden file of metric names checked into the repo; removing or renaming an entry fails CI unless an accompanying upcaster exists.

Unit coherence is the mechanism ADR-0007 binding rule 2 relies on: "the compiler rejects unit-incoherent comparisons (`atr(14) > 5 %` is a compile error unless an explicit conversion is present)". The unit taxonomy published here is what E35-T04 checks against, so it must be exhaustive and every metric must carry one — a metric with a null unit is a CI failure.

Response is large and static-ish: serve with a strong ETag derived from the registry content hash plus the caller's permission set (permissions change what is marked available), and a `Cache-Control: private, max-age=60`. SCR-081 states the vocabulary is cached client-side; the ETag is what makes an editor reload cheap.

The `vocabulary-unavailable (engine offline)` state named in SCR-081 must be distinguishable: return `503` with the standard problem document rather than an empty catalogue, so the editor shows the engine-offline state instead of an editor with no metrics.

## Test plan
Unit: projection of a fake registry into vocabulary entries; unit taxonomy exhaustiveness; permission-dependent availability marking; ETag stability and change-on-content-change.
Completeness tests: every `Action.type` in the IR enum has a parameter schema and a permission declaration; every trigger type has its companion-field rule; every registry metric has a descriptor (the regression guard scenario); the golden metric-name file matches.
Contract: response validates against the `RuleVocabulary` schema in `22-api-openapi.yaml`; the served `rule-ir.json` validates the whole fixture corpus.
Integration: vocabulary scoped to an unrecorded symbol returns the disabled entries with dependencies.
Coverage >=85%.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

Specific to this ticket: the vocabulary is an information-disclosure surface — it must not leak account ids, account names or symbol permissions the caller lacks. `x-rbac` is `scope: none` for the catalogue itself, but the *availability* annotations are computed from the caller's grants, so the response varies per user and must not be cached in a shared cache (hence `Cache-Control: private`). Action permission declarations here are advisory for the UI only; the authoritative check happens in E35-S03/S04 at execution time — never trust the client to have respected them.

## Accessibility notes

title: Implement the semantic validator and the compile and validate endpoints
body:
## Context
This is the contract both editors live against and the hinge of the round-trip guarantee. `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/compile` "accepts either editor's native model and returns canonical IR plus its `ir_hash`. Compiling the form model and the graph model of the same rule MUST produce an identical hash; that equality is the round-trip guarantee asserted by the contract tests in 24-internal-schemas.md §11.4." `POST /api/v1/rules/validate` is the static analysis both editors call on debounce, checking "schema conformance, variable existence, type compatibility, action-parameter completeness, unreachable branches, missing guards, and the `require_native_stop` invariant", returning errors **and** warnings — warnings do not block saving but do block arming.

SCR-081's round-trip indicator has four designed states driven by this endpoint on every save and every editor-mode switch, and a mismatch is an audited event (`rule.roundtrip_verified`, `rule.roundtrip_mismatch_resolved`) because "a mismatch resolution can silently change what an armed rule does".

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Compiler front-ends**: `compile_form(model) -> IR` and `compile_graph(model) -> IR`, both targeting the single `packages/rule_ir` representation from E35-T01. The form model is the linear restricted subset; the graph model is the general DAG.
- **Decompilers**: `to_form_model(ir)` (valid only when `form_compatible(ir)`) and `to_graph_model(ir)` with auto-layout when no `graph_layout` exists — these are what make the round trip closed rather than one-way.
- **Graph well-formedness**: reject cycles (ADR-0007 binding rule 4 — "graphs must be acyclic and must reduce to a single boolean condition plus an ordered action list; cycles and multiple sinks are compile errors with a clear message"), report the cycle as a path of node ids, reject orphan nodes that reach no action and dangling required input ports, listing each by node id for the editor's jump-to-node error list (US-RULE-005 scenarios).
- **Node-only construct marking**: when a graph uses a construct outside the form subset (shared sub-expression fan-out, nested arithmetic, `n_of`, multi-level nesting), record it in the IR at creation time so the form editor renders it read-only rather than discovering it at switch time (US-RULE-005 final scenario, US-RULE-006 read-only fallback).
- **Semantic validator** producing `RuleValidationResult` (`valid`, `errors[]`, `warnings[]` each with `path`/`code`/`message`, `referenced_variables`, `referenced_actions`, `estimated_evaluations_per_minute`): metric existence against E35-T03's vocabulary; **unit/type coherence** per ADR-0007 binding rule 2 (`atr(14) > 5%` is an error without an explicit conversion); operator applicability; action parameter completeness against the per-action schemas; unreachable branches; missing guards (`guard_missing` warning when no cooldown is set on a high-frequency trigger); the `require_native_stop` invariant; and the **feedback-loop guard** from §11.7 — "a rule whose own action would re-trigger it is rejected at save time by static analysis".
- **Safety-class warnings** are a distinct class, because `PUT /rules/{id}/mode` refuses to arm with open warnings of class `safety`.
- `POST /api/v1/rules/validate` and `POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/compile` handlers with their documented RBAC, plus the `rule_ir_invalid` (422) error code already registered in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- The `422` response returns the offending JSON path, never a bare failure.

## Out of scope
- Persisting a compiled version — **E35-S01**.
- Evaluating the IR — **E35-S02**.
- Rendering validation results — E36 (CMP-234 ValidationPanel) and E37.
- Conflict detection *between* rules — **E35-S07** (this ticket validates one rule in isolation).
- Auto-layout aesthetics beyond a deterministic, semantics-preserving arrangement — refinement is E37.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Both editors compile to the same hash
  Given the form model and the graph model of one semantically identical rule
  When each is posted to POST /api/v1/rules/{ruleId}/compile
  Then both responses carry the same ir_hash and an empty issues list

Scenario: Unit-incoherent comparison is a compile error (failure case)
  Given a condition comparing atr(14), a price-unit metric, to a percent literal with no explicit conversion
  When the IR is validated
  Then valid is false and an error names the offending node path with code type_mismatch and an explanation naming both units

Scenario: A cycle is refused with a readable path (failure case)
  Given a graph model whose node output feeds back into one of its own upstream inputs
  When it is compiled
  Then a 422 rule_ir_invalid is returned naming the cycle as an ordered list of node ids
  And no IR is produced

Scenario: A self-retriggering rule is refused at save time (edge case)
  Given a rule triggered on_order_fill whose only action places an order in the same scope
  When it is validated
  Then the feedback-loop guard raises a safety-class error explaining the loop

Scenario: Warnings inform but do not block saving
  Given a rule with no cooldown on an on_price_update trigger
  When it is validated
  Then valid is true with a guard_missing warning at path guards.cooldown_seconds
  And the rule can be saved but cannot be armed while a safety-class warning is open

Scenario: Graph-only construct is marked at compile time, not at switch time
  Given a graph fanning one node output into two consumers
  When it is compiled
  Then the resulting IR records the node-only marking so the form editor renders that sub-tree read-only on first load
```

## Technical notes / design
Compilation pipeline, both front-ends: parse editor model -> build IR nodes -> topological check -> canonicalise (E35-T01) -> hash -> validate -> return `{ir, ir_hash, issues}`.

The **round-trip diff** required by SCR-081/SCR-088 is produced here: when the caller supplies both the form model and the stored graph representation, the endpoint compiles both and, on divergence, returns a structured diff of the two canonical documents. US-RULE-006 requires this to be downloadable and the switch to be **aborted** on mismatch, leaving the rule untouched and emitting a high-severity telemetry event — the server must therefore never auto-reconcile a mismatch.

`estimated_evaluations_per_minute` is computed from the trigger type, debounce and (for `on_bar_close`) the timeframe; it is what lets the UI warn about a rule that would evaluate thousands of times a minute before it is armed.

Auto-layout (`to_graph_model` when `graph_layout` is absent) must be **deterministic** — same IR gives the same coordinates — otherwise opening a form-authored rule in the graph editor twice would produce two different `presentation` blocks and confuse the user (though not the hash, since layout is excluded). A simple layered Sugiyama-style pass over the DAG is sufficient.

Every error and warning carries a stable machine `code` (`type_mismatch`, `unknown_metric`, `missing_action_param`, `guard_missing`, `unreachable_branch`, `cycle_detected`, `orphan_node`, `dangling_port`, `feedback_loop`, `native_stop_violation`, `permission_required`) because the editors key their inline messages and jump-to-node behaviour off the code, not the prose.

## Test plan
Unit (>=90%): one case per error/warning code, valid and invalid; compile/decompile round trip per fixture; auto-layout determinism; cycle detection over self-loop, two-node loop and long loop; orphan and dangling-port detection; `estimated_evaluations_per_minute` arithmetic per trigger type.
Property-based: for every generated form-subset IR, `compile_form(to_form_model(ir))` has the same hash as `ir`; for every generated IR, `compile_graph(to_graph_model(ir))` has the same hash. This is the core of the R3 exit-criterion-5 machinery; **E35-Q02** scales it to 10 000 documents per run.
Contract: `/rules/validate` and `/rules/{ruleId}/compile` request/response shapes against `22-api-openapi.yaml`, including the documented examples (`withWarning`, `invalid`) verbatim.
Integration: validation against a live vocabulary including an unrecorded symbol and an estimated metric.
Perf: 100-node compile + diff p95 <=500 ms (SCR-081); validate p95 <=300 ms.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

Specific to this ticket: the validator is a **safety gate**, not a convenience. Two checks are security-relevant and must have dedicated tests that would fail loudly if removed: the `require_native_stop` invariant (no compiled rule may produce a plan that removes the native exchange-side SL — ADR-0007 binding rule 7, ADR-0008) and the `only_tighten` default on stop modifications (setting `only_tighten=false` requires the `rules.loosen_stop` permission and the Owner role). Compilation must be bounded: reject documents exceeding the schema's node limits before walking them, so a hostile model cannot make the compiler itself the DoS vector. Security review label required.

## Accessibility notes
No UI, but the message text produced here is read verbatim by screen readers through CMP-234 ValidationPanel and the editors' inline errors. Messages must name the row/node in words ("Row 2 is missing a value.", "`position_side` compares to long/short, not a number." — the exact examples in SCR-081), never rely on colour or position alone, and never surface a raw stack trace or JSON pointer as the only explanation.

## Performance notes
Budgets: validate round trip <=300 ms; compile + round-trip diff <=500 ms p95 for a 100-node rule (both from the SCR-081 performance note). Validation runs on debounce, not per keystroke — the server must not assume otherwise but should stay cheap enough that it would not matter. Benchmarked in CI with a 100-node fixture.

## Observability
`rule_compile_total{editor,result}`, `rule_compile_duration_seconds`, `rule_validate_total{valid}`, `rule_roundtrip_mismatch_total` (high-severity; alerts). Audit `rule.validated` and `rule.roundtrip_verified {result: identical|graph_only_construct|mismatch|unverified}`. A mismatch logs both hashes and stores the diff for support.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by a named automated test.
- [ ] Coverage: rule-engine package >=90% line (R3 local policy, roadmap §7.4), other backend >=85%, frontend >=80%; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Docs updated where behaviour diverged: `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §11, `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4; ADR-0007 amended if an IR semantic changed.
- [ ] SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit) and SCA (pip-audit/npm audit) clean or triaged with accepted-risk sign-off.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] PR(s) <=400 LOC diff, merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (`rules_global_enabled`; `rules.graph_editor` where relevant).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo), or marked non-demoable infra-adjacent with Architect concurrence.

## Dependencies

title: Add IR version upcasters and the built-in system rules
body:
## Context
Two small but load-bearing pieces that the rest of the epic assumes exist.

**Migrations.** US-RULE-001's third scenario: a rule stored under an older IR version "is migrated on load, the migration is logged, and the rule remains disarmed until reviewed". Its NFR adds that "migrations are pure functions with a golden-file test per version pair". ADR-0007 lists IR versioning as an accepted negative consequence, mitigated "by a `version` field with explicit upcasters and a test that loads every historical fixture rule". `ir_version` is `{"const": 1}` today, so this ticket builds the machinery and its first no-op case rather than a migration nobody needs yet — the cost of adding it later, once armed rules exist in production, is far higher.

**Built-in system rules.** `24-internal-schemas.md` §11.8 specifies eight shipped, non-deletable, individually toggleable rules that "exist so the dangerous basics are correct out of the box rather than hand-built by every user".

## Scope / Deliverables
- An upcaster registry: `upcast(ir, from_version, to_version)` composed of pure per-step functions, applied on load, logged once as its own version entry, leaving the rule **disarmed until reviewed**.
- Golden-file test harness: one fixture per version pair, plus a test that loads every historical fixture in `tests/fixtures/rule_ir/` under the current engine.
- The eight built-in rules from §11.8, seeded as non-deletable rows with their documented defaults:
  - `sys.native_sl_watchdog` — position without a native SL >10 s -> attach fallback + critical alert. **Always on, cannot be disabled.**
  - `sys.daily_loss_lockout` — `realised_pnl_today <= -max_daily_loss` -> `halt_new_orders` until next UTC day + notify. On, per-profile threshold.
  - `sys.max_positions_guard` — `open_positions_count >= max_open_positions` -> veto new entries via `pre_trade_check`. On.
  - `sys.clock_drift_block` — `ClockSyncEvent.action == block_trading` -> halt order entry. **On, cannot be disabled.**
  - `sys.stale_feed_block` — book/trade feed stale >5 s -> `pre_trade_check` veto. On.
  - `sys.breakeven_at_1r` — `unrealised_r_multiple >= 1` -> `move_to_breakeven(2 ticks)`, `once_per=position`. Off by default.
  - `sys.time_stop` — `time_in_trade_ms > max` and `unrealised_r < 0.2` -> flatten + tag. Off.
  - `sys.funding_flip_flatten` — funding flips against the position beyond a bps threshold after a minimum hold -> flatten + tag. Off.
- Enforcement that a `sys.*` rule cannot be deleted, cannot be renamed, and that the two "cannot disable" rules reject a mode change to `disabled` from any path including a crafted API call.
- Classification of `sys.*` rules into the risk-control precedence band used by **E35-S07**.

## Out of scope
- The risk-cap computation and lockout mechanics the daily-loss rule triggers — **E39**.
- The clock-sync event source — **E08**; the native-SL attachment mechanism — **E32**. The built-ins reference them.
- A second IR version — none exists yet; this ticket builds the path, not a hypothetical migration.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A migrated rule does not arm itself
  Given a rule stored under an older ir_version
  When it is loaded
  Then it is migrated by pure upcaster functions, the migration is recorded once as its own version entry
  And the rule remains disarmed until a human reviews it

Scenario: Every historical fixture still loads (regression guard)
  Given the full corpus in tests/fixtures/rule_ir/
  When the current engine loads each one
  Then all load successfully under the current ir_version, or fail with a named missing upcaster rather than a parse error

Scenario: Safety built-ins cannot be turned off (failure case)
  Given sys.native_sl_watchdog or sys.clock_drift_block
  When any path including a crafted API request attempts to disable or delete it
  Then the request is refused with 403, no state changes, and an audit row is written

Scenario: Optional built-ins are off by default
  Given a freshly seeded installation
  Then sys.breakeven_at_1r, sys.time_stop and sys.funding_flip_flatten are present and disabled
  And sys.daily_loss_lockout, sys.max_positions_guard and sys.stale_feed_block are enabled

Scenario: Built-ins outrank user rules (edge case)
  Given a user rule configured at the highest priority conflicting with sys.daily_loss_lockout
  When both would act
  Then the system rule wins and the override is logged
```

## Technical notes / design
Upcasters are pure `dict -> dict` functions registered against `(from, to)` and composed transitively, so adding version 3 later requires only the 2->3 step. They run **before** pydantic parsing, because a stored document of an older version may not parse under the current models at all — this ordering is the usual mistake.

Built-ins are seeded by migration with fixed UUIDs so they are stable across environments and referencable from documentation and runbooks. They are ordinary IR documents — they must not be special-cased in the evaluator, which would create a second, untested execution path. Their non-deletability is a repository and API concern, enforced by a `is_system` marker plus an API guard, not by the engine.

`sys.native_sl_watchdog` interacts with the OMS's own 2-second SL attachment deadline (`24-internal-schemas.md` §8.8): the watchdog is the 10-second second line of defence, not a replacement. Both must exist; a test asserts the watchdog fires when the OMS path has failed.

## Test plan
Unit (>=90%): upcaster composition across a synthetic 1->2->3 chain; pure-function property (no I/O, idempotent); pre-parse ordering; golden file per version pair.
Corpus test: every fixture loads under the current engine.
Built-ins: one behavioural test per rule against recorded fixtures asserting it fires when it should and stays silent otherwise; default on/off state after a fresh seed; non-deletability and non-disableability including crafted API attempts.
Integration: `sys.native_sl_watchdog` firing when a position has existed >10 s without a native SL, with the OMS attachment path stubbed as failed.

## Security notes
Threat sources: `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (STRIDE per epic) and the E35 model produced by E35-X01.
- **Tampering** — the stored IR decides what an armed rule does; every version carries `ir_hash` (sha256 of canonical JSON) and the arming audit record embeds it, so "what exactly was armed" is provable.
- **Elevation of privilege** — a rule must never act on an account its author cannot trade; scope is enforced at *runtime on every action*, not only at save time (US-RULE-007 NFR).
- **Denial of service** — a pathological IR must not stall the evaluator: node counts are bounded by the JSON Schema (max 32 boolean children, max 10 actions, max 8 arithmetic operands) and every evaluation is time-boxed by `limits.evaluation_timeout_ms`.
- **Repudiation** — `rule_events` is append-only via the `trg_re_append`/`forbid_mutation` trigger.
- **Code execution** — the IR is data, never code (ADR-0007 R1): no `eval`, no expression strings parsed at runtime, no user scripting. Any PR introducing dynamic evaluation is an automatic reject.
Data classification: rule IR is *internal*; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` can contain account equity and position data — *financial/confidential*, never logged at INFO in plaintext to shared sinks. Security review label required.

Specific to this ticket: `sys.native_sl_watchdog` and `sys.clock_drift_block` are safety controls whose disablement must be impossible, not merely discouraged — the negative test is required. Migration is a tampering surface: an upcaster that silently changes semantics would alter what an armed rule does, which is why a migrated rule is force-disarmed until reviewed and the migration is recorded as its own auditable version entry with its own `ir_hash`.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend. The built-in rules' names and descriptions are user-visible in the rules list and the templates gallery and must be written in plain language (the user sees `sys.breakeven_at_1r` as "Move stop to breakeven at 1R").

## Performance notes
Upcasting runs on load only and must add <=5 ms to loading a rule. The built-ins are ordinary rules and consume the ordinary evaluation budget; `sys.stale_feed_block` and `sys.clock_drift_block` run on the `pre_trade_check` path and therefore share its tighter 25 ms budget.

## Observability
`rule_ir_migrations_total{from,to}`, `rule_system_rule_fires_total{rule}`, and a `critical` alert whenever `sys.native_sl_watchdog` fires — it firing means the primary SL attachment path failed, which is an incident, not routine.

## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires that the plan documents "reflect final shipped behavior (not the original proposal) if they diverged during implementation". E35 implements a large, precisely-specified surface across five documents and two ADRs; some divergence between the September 2026 specification and what actually ships in S14-S17 is certain, and an undocumented divergence in the rule engine is expensive, because E36, E37, E40 and E41 all read these documents as their contract.

## Scope / Deliverables

- Reconcile `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.4 against the applied migration (constraints, indexes, retention).
- Reconcile `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/rules*` and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §15.6 against the implemented handlers and frames; regenerate examples from real responses so the documented examples are true rather than plausible.
- Amend **ADR-0007** with a Consequences-in-practice section, or file a superseding ADR if any binding rule changed; cross-link **ADR-0016** from E35-K01.
- Update `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-084..089 and `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-154..159/233/234 where the built behaviour differs from the catalogue entry, in coordination with E35-D06 design QA.
- Write the operator runbook section for the rule engine: what "rules paused — feed degraded" means, how to inspect a firing, how to force-disarm everything, what to do when `sys.native_sl_watchdog` fires, and how the retention job is monitored.
- Confirm `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` US-RULE rows still point at the right screens and components.

## Out of scope
- User-facing help content and onboarding copy — E48 docs epic in R5.
- Rewriting the research digests — they are historical records.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

Scenario: API examples are real
  Given the documented examples in 22-api-openapi.yaml for the rules operations
  When each is replayed against the running service
```

## Technical notes / design
Do this as a checklist PR with the diff organised document by document, so a reviewer can verify each claim independently. Where the OpenAPI examples are regenerated, capture them from the contract-test fixtures rather than hand-editing, which is how examples drift in the first place.

title: STRIDE threat model for the rule engine IR, compiler and runtime
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requires a STRIDE threat model per epic, and the R3 quality gates name **E35** among the six epics (with E27, E29, E34, E39, E42) whose model must have all Critical/High findings closed before the train closes.

E35 deserves that attention for a specific reason: it is the only subsystem in the product that can place, modify and cancel orders **without a human present**. Everything else — the ticket, chart trading, DOM clicks — has a person at the moment of action. A rule has a person only at authoring time, possibly weeks earlier, possibly with different permissions than they hold now.

The architecture already carries deliberate mitigations that the model must validate rather than re-derive: the IR is data not code (ADR-0007 R1), actions reach the market only through the OMS so profile and risk caps apply afterwards (§11.7), scope is enforced at runtime on every action (US-RULE-007 NFR), and the firing log is append-only (§3.4.3).

## Scope / Deliverables
- A STRIDE analysis over the E35 data-flow diagram, decomposed by trust boundary: editor → compile/validate API → rule store → evaluator → action executor → OMS; and evaluator → metric bus; and evaluator → firing log → WS subscribers.
- **Spoofing**: can a rule act as a user it is not? Session and step-up handling on arming; the identity attached to rule-originated orders; whether `emit_signal`/`on_signal` can be used to cross a permission boundary between two users' rules.
- **Tampering**: stored IR modification (mitigated by `ir_hash` in the arming audit); `graph_layout`/`form_model` fields excluded from the hash — can anything semantic be smuggled into them?; jsonb key-order pitfalls; import bundles as a tampering vector; whether an upcaster can silently change semantics (mitigated by force-disarm on migration).
- **Repudiation**: append-only `rule_events`; whether a firing can occur without a corresponding audit row; whether the log can be made to disagree with what the engine did (this is also exploratory charter 5 in E35-Q07 — coordinate).
- **Information disclosure**: `rule_runs.input_snapshot` contains account equity and PnL; WS `rules` subscription-option intersection with grants; the vocabulary endpoint's per-user availability annotations; export bundles; whether a 403 reveals the existence of an account.
- **Denial of service**: pathological IR (node bounds, temporal window allocation, `n_of` at the bound); many rules per user; simulation as a resource sink; log write amplification; whether a user can make the `pre_trade_check` path slow enough to breach the 300 ms submit budget and thereby degrade *all* trading.
- **Elevation of privilege**: acting on ungranted accounts; `targets: all_accounts`; `only_tighten=false` and `widen_stop` requiring `rules.loosen_stop` plus Owner; arming preconditions bypass; whether a manager can author a rule that the owner's session effectively executes.
- **Abuse cases specific to automation**: a rule authored to fire at maximum rate as a self-inflicted rate-limit exhaustion; a rule chain (`emit_signal` → `on_signal`) engineered as an amplification loop; a rule that arms itself via `enable_rule` targeting another rule.
- Findings logged with severity (CVSS-informed), owner and disposition; mitigations traced to the specific ticket implementing them.

## Out of scope
- The editors' own threat surface (XSS in a node label, for instance) — E36/E37, though the model should note the boundary.
- OMS, key vault, RBAC and kill-switch threat models — E29, E27, E09, E39 own those; this model consumes their conclusions rather than repeating them.
- Penetration testing — **E43** in R4.
- Implementing mitigations — they are filed against the owning engineering tickets.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every trust boundary is analysed
  Given the E35 data-flow diagram
  When the STRIDE analysis completes
  Then every boundary has each of the six categories considered, with either a threat and a mitigation or a recorded reason it does not apply

Scenario: Mitigations are traced to code, not to prose
  Given each identified threat with a claimed mitigation
  When the model is reviewed
  Then each mitigation names the ticket and the test that proves it, rather than asserting the design handles it

Scenario: Automation-specific abuse cases are covered (edge case)
  Given the abuse cases unique to unattended execution
  When the model is reviewed by the Architect
  Then rate-exhaustion, signal-amplification and cross-user rule-chaining are each analysed with a stated control

Scenario: An unmitigated High blocks the train (failure case)
  Given a High-severity finding with no mitigation
  When the R3 gate is assessed
  Then the finding blocks the gate until fixed or accepted by the Owner with a written rationale
```

## Technical notes / design
Build the model from the real data-flow rather than the idealised one: include the `pre_trade_check` synchronous path, the `emit_signal` bus, the import/export boundary and the WS fan-out, all of which are easy to omit from a diagram drawn from the architecture document alone.

Two threats deserve particular attention because they are specific to this epic and have no analogue elsewhere in the product:
1. **Time-of-authoring versus time-of-execution permission drift.** A rule authored with a grant that is later revoked is the central elevation-of-privilege case; E35-S04 is the mitigation and the model should state precisely what "runtime enforcement" must cover to be sufficient.
2. **The `pre_trade_check` path as a shared-fate component.** A slow or failing rule on this path degrades order submission for everyone, not just its author. Consider whether a per-rule failure should eject that rule from the path rather than slowing it.

Record the model in the standard template used by the other R3 epics so the six models can be reviewed comparably at the train gate.

## Test plan
The model's assertions are validated by tests owned elsewhere: E35-Q07 charters 1, 5 and 6; E35-X02's abuse-case suite; E35-Q05's fail-safe chaos scenarios. Where the model identifies a threat with no corresponding test, filing that test is part of this ticket's output.

## Security notes
This ticket *is* the security deliverable. Classification of the epic's data: rule IR **internal**; `rule_runs.input_snapshot` **financial/confidential**; audit and firing log **evidentiary, append-only**; no PII or secrets are stored by this epic, and the model must confirm that no path causes a credential to be logged or exported.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — analysis artefact. One note the model should carry: security controls that depend on a user reading a warning (the arming dialog's plain-language restatement) must be accessible, or the control fails for some users — cross-referenced to E35-D04 and E35-Q06.

## Performance notes
The DoS analysis intersects with E35-Q04's benchmarks; where the model identifies a resource-exhaustion threat, the corresponding benchmark becomes the evidence that the control holds — coordinate so a threat does not go untested because it looked like a performance concern.

## Observability
The model specifies which security-relevant events must be observable: arming (high severity), live-environment scope changes, `only_tighten=false` usage, `targets: all_accounts` usage, import/export, quarantine on schema violation, and auto-disable. Any event the model requires but the implementation lacks is filed against the owning ticket.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts committed under `docs/security/e35/` and linked from `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`.
- [ ] Every finding triaged with a severity, an owner and a disposition (fixed / accepted-risk with Owner sign-off / deferred with a dated ticket).
- [ ] No Critical or High finding left open — the R3 quality gate names E35 explicitly and requires all Critical/High closed before the train ends.
- [ ] Security engineer review comment posted on this ticket.
- [ ] Relevant findings reflected in `docs/plan/32-risk-register.md`.
- [ ] Presented at the security review; the Architect and rule-engine backend lead acknowledge the model.

## Dependencies
Blocked by **E35-T04**, by which point the compile/validate contract and the epic's real data flow are settled. Feeds **E35-X02**, **E35-X03**, **E35-Q07** and the R3 security gate. Consumes the models from **E09**, **E27**, **E29** and **E39** rather than duplicating them.
